Assess the patient's ability for informed consent
questions.explanation:
The priority is assessing the patient's ability for informed consent because:
1. Patient autonomy must be respected
2. Emergency doesn't automatically override consent requirements
3. Brother may not have legal authority
4. Must determine if patient can participate in decision-making

questions.questionText: A married woman who has five children living in a definite community makes great effort to fulfill basic needs of the family. The woman manages the family by selling vegetables at the market far from home. The husband does not support the woman; instead, he always comes late at night, and also slaps and kicks her. What is the most likely type of violence in this case?
questions.explanation:
This is Physical abuse because:
1. Involves actual physical harm (slapping, kicking)
2. Different from economic which controls finances
3. Psychological would involve emotional manipulation
4. Sexual abuse isn't mentioned in scenario

questions.questionText: After attending a wedding ceremony, many people showed signs of sudden onset of vomiting, watery diarrhea, fever and abdominal cramp within a short period of time. The people who experienced those signs were taken to a nearby hospital to get emergency medical treatment and the diagnosis of all the people was food intoxication. What is the most likely type of outbreak in this scenario?
questions.explanation:
This is a Point common source epidemic because:
1. Single exposure event (wedding meal)
2. Short incubation period
3. Cases clustered in time
4. Different from continuous source which would have ongoing exposure

questions.questionText: A two-year-old child was brought to a health center with complaints of cough and fever of three days duration. On examination, oxygen saturation is 95 percent with a respiratory rate of 36/min. What is the most likely management for this child?
options: Refer the child urgently to the hospital after giving first line drugs
Advise the mother to give fluid remedies
Provide bronchodilators and send home with appointment
questions.explanation:
The correct management is providing Amoxicillin because:
1. Symptoms suggest bacterial infection
2. Oxygen saturation is normal
3. Respiratory rate is only mildly elevated
4. WHO guidelines recommend antibiotics for persistent fever and cough

questions.questionText: A three-day-old male neonate was brought by his father after his mother died due to maternal complication. A father needs health education about formula feeding. What is the most appropriate health education message for the father?
options: Sterilizing bottles and nipples for 30 seconds with lap water
Dilute with extra water to extend the amount of formula
Use bottled water without fluoride for mixing infant formula
Always follow manufacturers instruction about preparation
questions.explanation:
The most appropriate education is to follow manufacturer's instructions because:
1. Ensures proper nutrition
2. Prevents over-dilution which can cause hyponatremia
3. Proper sterilization requires boiling water
4. Bottled water isn't necessarily safer

questions.questionText: An instructor showed students about the procedure of female catheterization. After the discussion, all students tried to do the procedure based on the steps. What is the most likely teaching method applied in this scenario?
questions.explanation:
This is Demonstration because:
1. Instructor showed procedure first
2. Students then practiced
3. Different from simulation which uses mannequins
4. Hands-on skill training method

questions.questionText: A nurse working at medical ward had five patients. One of the patients was on end stage of life. After many supports, the doctors confirmed that the patient will not survive and the nurse also confirmed that. Then, the nurse withholds basic care for the patient and focused only on the other patients. Meanwhile, the head nurse saw the patient, gave warning to the nurse and ordered to continue the necessary cares until death is confirmed. What is the most likely reason for the order by the head nurse in this case?
options: The nurse feared the family complaint that will happen after death
The patient should get dignified care irrespective of the condition
It is not human authority to predict death of the patient
The nurse suspected the physicians evidence
questions.explanation:
The reason is dignified care because:
1. All patients deserve compassionate care
2. Withholding basic care is unethical
3. Comfort measures should continue
4. Doesn't matter if death is imminent

questions.questionText: A two-year-old child was presented to a clinic with runny nose and barking cough. Physical examination revealed hoarseness, respiratory rate of 38/min, and body temperature of 36.8 degree contiguous. Otherwise, the child has clear chest sounds. What is the most likely eucogic agent for this case?
questions.explanation:
Most likely Para influenza virus because:
1. Causes croup (barking cough)
2. Accounts for most cases of laryngotracheobronchitis
3. RSV typically causes bronchiolitis
4. Rhino virus usually causes cold symptoms

questions.questionText: A seven-year-old child was brought to a clinic with fever and pain on urination of one day duration. Examination revealed flank pain. There were no microscopic urine bacteria. Then, a nurse discharged the patient with PO medication and appointed for after seven days. What is the most likely medication given by the nurse?
questions.explanation:
Most likely Co-trimoxazole because:
1. First line for UTIs in children
2. Broad spectrum coverage
3. Effective against common uropathogens
4. Can be given orally

questions.questionText: A director wanted to improve service quality of a hospital at the end of the budget year. To achieve the plan, he fulfills different resources and helps the staff to get ready for promotion. What is the most likely factor promoting staff motivation in this scenario?
questions.explanation:
The factor is Advancement because:
1. Involves promotion opportunities
2. Career growth motivates staff
3. Different from achievement which is task completion
4. Responsibility would involve more duties

questions.questionText: A two-hour-old newborn developed a brief and strange movement. On evaluation, the airway was clear, and there was normal breathing pattern and adequate circulation. Smacking and breast feeding like lip movement and eye deviation were noted frequently. What is the most appropriate primary nursing intervention in this case?
questions.explanation:
Priority is treating hypoglycemia because:
1. Early neonatal hypoglycemia presents with:
   - Jitteriness
   - Poor feeding
   - Lip smacking
   - Eye rolling
2. Blood glucose should be checked immediately
3. Normal newborn glucose should be >45 mg/dL
4. Risk factors include:
   - First 24-48 hours of life
   - Delayed feeding
   - Maternal diabetes
5. Treatment with glucose is safe and immediately effective
6. Rule out hypoglycemia before considering anticonvulsants

questions.questionText: A 35-year-old man came to a psychiatric clinic with sleep disturbance for the last nine months. He believes that his family wants to kill him by poisoned food because he is famous. He has weight loss as a result of refusing to eat and drink. He is happy most of the day; he is extravagant, dances alone and has sleep disturbance. He has self-care deficiency and social isolation. On examination, his blood pressure is 80/40mmHg, and pulse rate is 100/min. What is the priority nursing intervention for this scenario?
options: Supplement diet with vitamins and minerals
questions.explanation:
Priority is administering medication because:
1. Patient has psychotic features
2. Medical instability (low BP)
3. Immediate safety concern
4. Other interventions can follow

questions.questionText: A new team has been created to manage acute feintie illness in a hospital. The team consists of 5 nurses, 2 health officers, 5 physicians and 2 detentors. The individuals in the team have refused to provide quality services for patients as per the standard. What is the most likely action of the individuals in this case?
questions.explanation:
They are Opposing because:
1. Resisting standard protocols
2. Not just observing but refusing
3. Different from initiating change
4. Actively working against standards

questions.questionText: A 56-year-old male patient came to a hospital with urinary tract obstruction. A physician decided to perform cystotomy and communicated with a nurse to take informed consent. After the nurse explained in detail about the disease and treatment alternatives for the patient, the nurse saw the sign of acceptance from the patient's facial expression. What is the best next step the nurse should do in this case?
options: Take the signature of the patient
Inform the physician the patient's acceptance
Give the patient a chance to talk to identify his need
questions.explanation:
Next step is obtaining signature because:
1. Facial expression isn't legal consent
2. Documentation required
3. Verifies understanding
4. Protects patient rights

questions.questionText: A head of a health center prioritized different health care services in order to decide the amount of materials and professionals needed for each department's activities. Then after, he engaged in assigning professionals, setting schedules, giving out materials, and preparing budgets according to their activities. What is the most likely role of a manager applied in this scenario?
questions.explanation:
Role is Resource allocator because:
1. Distributing materials
2. Assigning personnel
3. Budget preparation
4. Core management function

questions.questionText: A instructor was writing from the syllabus during the first day of a class 'Based on the course objectives, all students will evaluate the knowledge, attitude and skills; those attending the course will evaluate the success of the course by taking oral examination, written test and practical exam.' What is the most appropriate component of course syllabus stated in this scenario?
questions.explanation:
This describes Assessment method because:
1. Outlines evaluation tools
2. Specifies knowledge/skills tested
3. Different from teaching methods
4. Core syllabus component

questions.questionText: A 20-year-old woman came to a clinic for family planning service. She never used any family planning method before. The nurse in charge greeted the client and started to provide counseling on family planning methods. But the woman was fearful to communicate her issue for the nurse. What is the most appropriate counseling principle the nurse should follow?
options: Provide information on the a clinic preference on family planning method
Explore the client's satisfaction with the method
Try to involve another nurse for discussion
Engage in two way communication with the client
questions.explanation:
The principle is two-way communication because:
1. Builds trust
2. Allows client to express concerns
3. More effective than one-way
4. Client-centered approach

questions.questionText: A child was brought to a health center with a complaint of tender swelling behind the ear. Body temperature showed 38 degree centigrade. The child had a history of recurrent upper respiratory infection. Then, the child was treated accordingly. What is the most appropriate treatment for this child?
questions.explanation:
Most appropriate is Amoxacillin PO because:
1. First line for otitis media
2. Covers common pathogens
3. Oral route preferred
4. IV only if severe

questions.questionText: A three-year-old child who had been on ART for three months was brought to a pediatric OPD due to weight loss. The child has no history of diarrhea, cough and body swelling. Physical examination showed that MUAC is 11.6cm, weight for height is between -2 and -3.2 score and there is no bilateral pitting edema. The child was treated for malnutrition for more than a month though there was no response yet. What is the most likely clinical stage of the child in this case?
questions.explanation:
Clinical Stage III because:
1. Significant weight loss
2. MUAC <11.5cm
3. No opportunistic infections
4. Meets WHO criteria

questions.questionText: A 40-year-old woman came to a psychiatric clinic with drowsiness, cardiac arrhythmia, weight gain and orthostatic hypotension after she took Amitriptyline 100mg PO per day. She cannot perform her daily activities due to the problem. What is the most appropriate management option in this case?
questions.explanation:
Decrease Amitriptyline dose because:
1. Shows signs of toxicity
2. Side effects affecting function
3. Gradual reduction safer
4. Monitor for improvement

questions.questionText: A 45-year-old male patient was brought to a hospital by his brother with complete leg fracture and profuse bleeding secondary to car accident. The surgeons decided that the patient's leg should be amputated at below the knee. The surgeons were busy by other cases and informed the nurse to prepare the patient immediately for operation. What is the most appropriate initial step in the preparation of the patient in this case?
options: Take informed consent from his brother
Clean a surgical site with iodine solution
Assess the patient's ability for informed consent
questions.explanation:
Assess ability for consent because:
1. Patient autonomy paramount
2. Emergency doesn't negate consent
3. Brother may not be legal proxy
4. Must determine capacity

questions.questionText: A married woman who has five children living in a definite community makes great effort to fulfill basic needs of the family. The woman manages the family by selling vegetables at the market far from home. The husband does not support the woman; instead, he always comes late at night, and also slaps and kicks her. What is the most likely type of violence in this case?
questions.explanation:
Physical abuse because:
1. Involves hitting (slapping/kicking)
2. Clear physical violence
3. Different from psychological
4. No sexual component mentioned

questions.questionText: A two-year-old child, who has a travel history to the lowland areas of Ethiopia, was brought to a clinic with a complaint of high grade fever. Blood smear test is not available. What is the most likely diagnosis in this case?
questions.explanation:
Most likely Malaria because:
1. Endemic in lowlands
2. High fever primary symptom
3. Travel history significant
4. Empirical treatment often given

questions.questionText: A seven-year-old child with a previous history of trauma to the right leg was brought to a pediatric OPD due to painful right leg swelling associated with high grade fever and malaise. On examination, erythematic and tender swelling with indistinct lateral margins was appreciated. What is the most likely skin disorder in this scenario?
questions.explanation:
Cellulitis because:
1. Trauma history
2. Fever and malaise
3. Erythema and swelling
4. Indistinct margins characteristic

questions.questionText: A 20-year-old woman has been admitted to a gynecology ward with complaints of fever and abdominal pain for the day. She looks sick and anxious, has white and rigors. She had gone through illegal abortion in the early back. On examination, her dad signs more temperature as a drug-use certificate, public rate of 25/min, and registration rate of 24/min. Please communicate message with doctors, and postulent vaginal discharge with tender uterus. What is the most priority nursing diagnosis in this case?
options: Risk for infection related to dilated cervix
Acute pain related to uterine chipping
Risk for deficient fluid volume related to bleeding
questions.explanation:
Priority is Risk for infection because:
1. Post-abortion complication
2. Fever and rigors
3. Tender uterus
4. Potential sepsis risk

questions.questionText: During curriculum development, an incumbent wanted to assess the availability of anti-tab equipment, reference and procedure books. In order to deliver the program effectively, What is the most likely component of curriculum stated in this case?
questions.explanation:
Learning resources because:
1. Equipment and books
2. Materials for teaching
3. Different from teaching methods
4. Core curriculum element

questions.questionText: A seven-year-old child suddenly started coughing and had a difficulty of breathing while eating. The mother immediately called for help and the neighbor nurse arrived soon. What is the most appropriate nursing intervention for this child?
options: Till position to open the airway
Give five times of Heimlich maneuver
questions.explanation:
Five back blows because:
1. First line for choking
2. Under age 8 protocol
3. Clears obstruction
4. Different from abdominal thrusts

questions.questionText: A clinical nurse gave health education to a community about prevention mechanisms of infectious disease. Then, all the community members practiced the prevention approaches of infectious diseases each day. The health status of the community was maintained. Finally, the community members gave a credit for the primary prevention. What is the most appropriate communication stage for this scenario?
questions.explanation:
Improving to health because:
1. Behavior change occurred
2. Health outcomes improved
3. Final stage of communication
4. Beyond just understanding

questions.questionText: A 28-year-old woman came to a gynecology OPD with complaints of fever and vaginal discharge of one week duration. She had offensive vaginal discharge and high grade fever. Physical examination revealed the presence of lower abdominal tenderness, cervical motion tenderness, adnexal tenderness and pelvic mass. Laboratory finding suggested leukocytosis of 11,500/mm3. What is the most likely diagnosis in this case?
questions.explanation:
Pelvic inflammatory disease because:
1. Fever and discharge
2. Cervical motion tenderness
3. Leukocytosis
4. Classic triad of symptoms

questions.questionText: A 20-year-old female patient came to a health center for abortion on the sixth week of Time left, t:12.03 The nurse identified that the reason of abortion was conflict with her boyfriend. On tumor assessment, she had sign of anemia, hopelessness, and suicidal ideation. What is the best mechanism in which the nurse can support the patient?
options: Refer to hospital for abortion where there is blood transfusion
Try to call her family, discuss with them to help her
Take informed consent, conduct abortion and provide bite acid
Provide counseling and give her iron sulphate
questions.explanation:
Counseling and iron because:
1. Addresses mental health
2. Treats anemia
3. Comprehensive care
4. Respects autonomy

questions.questionText: A medical ward team leader is following whether or not the nursing care services are being delivered according to the standard performance using checklist. Furthermore, he measures and evaluates each activities based on the standard indicators and gives feedback to each staff members. What is the most likely management function practiced by the leader?
questions.explanation:
Controlling function because:
1. Monitoring performance
2. Using checklists
3. Providing feedback
4. Quality assurance

questions.questionText: A fourth year nursing student wanted to assess the nutritional status of a mother and measured her weight which was 56kg and height 1.65 meter in order to determine body mass index of the mother. What is the most likely nutritional assessment method applied in this case?
questions.explanation:
Anthropometric method because:
1. Uses weight/height
2. BMI calculation
3. Objective measurement
4. Different from dietary recall

questions.questionText: A 35-year-old man has been brought by his wife to a psychiatry department with symptoms of sleep disturbance and refusal to eat for the last seven months. The patient stated that his wife wants to kill him and he sees that his wife may put something on his food. He also hears that his friends were calling his name and insulting him. His family and the community have good support. His symptoms have become worsen when he gets into chewing chat and drinking alcohol. What is the most likely cause of the patient's condition in this scenario?
questions.explanation:
Substance abuse because:
1. Chat and alcohol use
2. Symptoms worsened with use
3. Psychotic features
4. Primary etiology

questions.questionText: A nurse working in surgical ward always tolerates the crying of patients due to severe pain during wound care. The nurse also advises other nurses not to insult patients, tells them that the patients are crying because of the pain. And the nurse tries to help the other nurses to understand and feel the patient's emotion. What component of dignified care best describes the nurse's behavior?
questions.explanation:
Empathy because:
1. Understanding patient feelings
2. Emotional connection
3. Different from sympathy (pity)
4. Core care component

questions.questionText: A nurse made an assessment for a patient admitted to a health center with chronic kidney disease, and found symptoms of mild distress, and significant impairment in social functioning. However, the patient had better self-care and coping skill. The nurse diagnosed the patient with adjustment disorder secondary to medical condition. What is the most appropriate nursing intervention in this case?
options: Teach deep breathing and relaxation techniques
Use supportive touch if client responds well
questions.explanation:
Establish social support because:
1. Addresses impairment
2. Builds coping resources
3. Patient has basic skills
4. Community integration

questions.questionText: A 30-year-old man came to a health center with a compliant of chills and abdominal g Time left 1:46:15 duration. The detail history showed that the patient had fever, headache and diarrhea for the last one week. On physical examination, there was enlargement of spleen. In addition the blood flow result was positive for hemo parasite. What is the most likely vector for disease transmission in the above case?
questions.explanation:
Female anopheles mosquito because:
1. Transmits malaria
2. Hemo parasite in blood
3. Fever/splenomegaly
4. Other vectors don't fit

questions.questionText: A newborn infant was brought to a clinic with complaints of exotien and red eye, pus discharging from both eyes and persistent crying of three days duration. The mother had multiple sexual partners. She also had hypertension, DM, and has been treated for malaria during pregnancy. A nurse admitted the newborn in neonatal ICU for further treatment. What is the most likely cause for the newborn problems?
questions.explanation:
Maternal STD because:
1. Ophthalmia neonatorum
2. Multiple partners risk
3. Pus discharge characteristic
4. Other conditions unrelated

questions.questionText: Investigators informed study participants before starting data collection saying: 'This data will not be disseminated to third party for any purpose without your voluntariness, and the principal investigator will keep the data in a computer with protected password. In addition there are no any identification parameters like name and others from the questionnaire.' What is the most appropriate principle of research ethics applied in this scenario?
questions.explanation:
Autonomy because:
1. Informed consent
2. Confidentiality
3. Participant control
4. Ethical research practice

questions.questionText: A neonate, who was diagnosed with neonatal sepsis, was admitted in a hospital. The nurse in charge examined the baby and the findings showed central cyanosis, chest in drawing, tachycardia and tachypnea. What is the most likely nursing diagnosis of this case?
questions.explanation:
Ineffective tissue perfusion because:
1. Cyanosis present
2. Sepsis complication
3. Circulatory compromise
4. Primary concern

questions.questionText: A 26-year-old Gravid II Para I pregnant woman came to ANC clinic with complaints of headache, dyspnea, and fatigue for three days. Her pulse rate was 78/min. Blood pressure was 100/60 mmHg and fetal heart rate was 140/min. On physical examination, she had pale conjunctiva and 32 weeks gestational age pregnancy. Her hemoglobin concentration was 10g/dl. What is the most likely indicative characteristic for the woman's problem?
questions.explanation:
Pale conjunctiva because:
1. Clinical sign of anemia
2. Hgb borderline low
3. Other symptoms nonspecific
4. Physical exam finding

questions.questionText: An infant was referred from private clinic to a health center with the diagnosis of severe anemia. On physical examination, the nurse found that infant's MUAC was less than 11.5cm, WFL less than -32 score, bilateral pitting edema and RBS less than 40mg/dl. What is the most appropriate management for this infant?
options: Admit the infant on OTP program
Give oral amoxicillin for seven days
Give folic acid supplement for anemia
Give 1st dose of antibiotic and refer
questions.explanation:
Antibiotic and refer because:
1. Severe malnutrition
2. Medical emergency
3. Needs hospital care
4. Stabilize first

questions.questionText: A graduate nurse took out DPT and TT vaccine from the refrigerator. Before administering those vaccines to children, the nurse checked the expiry date, VVM and reconstituted the vaccine. What is the most likely next step the nurse should do before vaccine administration?
options: Wash hands with soap and water
Explain the procedure to the mother
Prepare the injection site with alcohol
questions.explanation:
Check immunization card because:
1. Verify previous doses
2. Prevent over-immunization
3. Documentation
4. Protocol requirement

questions.questionText: ______ is a population about which the researcher intends to generalize the study findings.
questions.explanation: The target population is the entire group a researcher is interested in studying and generalizing findings to. Other options refer to subsets or specific groups within the target population.

questions.questionText: 19-year-old MTU student came to gynecology OPD after she had unprotected sexual intercourse 40 hours ago. She is unsure of when her last menstrual period was as her periods are irregular. Her regular contraceptive method is the male condom. What is the first step in management?
options: Refer her to a psychiatrist for evaluation and counseling.
questions.explanation: Emergency contraception is most effective when taken within 72 hours after unprotected intercourse. Since it's been 40 hours, this should be the immediate intervention to prevent potential pregnancy, given her irregular cycles and recent exposure.

questions.questionText: A 17-year-old high school student was raped in Mizan Aman town 4 hours back. Which are antibiotics of your choice to prevent this patient from acquiring STDs?
questions.explanation: This combination covers common STDs: Ceftriaxone for gonorrhea, Doxycycline for chlamydia, and Metronidazole for trichomoniasis. The other combinations either lack coverage for key pathogens or include inappropriate antibiotics.

questions.questionText: A 25-year-old G3 P2 mother at term presented to MCH of MTURH with gush of fluid per vagina of 10 minutes. The medical intern working at ANC clinic did per vaginal examination and felt a pulsatile cord in the vagina before the fetal head. The cervical dilatation is 2-3cm station is at 0. The most appropriate intervention would be:
options: Try to return the cord to the uterine cavity and send the mother to labor ward
Fill the bladder with saline and transfer for immediate delivery
Put in knee-chest position and transfer fast to labor ward for emergency cesarean section
Tell the mother to go to labor ward for delivery
questions.explanation: This describes umbilical cord prolapse, an obstetric emergency. Knee-chest position relieves pressure on the cord, while immediate C-section is needed to prevent fetal hypoxia/death from cord compression.

questions.questionText: Which vital signs should be monitored for a patient with pneumonia?
questions.explanation: Pneumonia primarily affects respiratory function (requiring RR monitoring) and typically causes fever (requiring temperature monitoring). Both are critical for assessing severity and treatment response.

title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Pharmacy (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Pharmacy (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: A physician orders diazepam 5mg po PRN. From the order which affects the treatment most?
questions.explanation: The frequency (PRN - as needed) has the most significant impact on treatment effectiveness. While dose, route, and drug choice are important, the PRN frequency means the medication is taken only when symptoms occur rather than on a regular schedule, making timing and frequency the critical factor that will determine therapeutic outcomes.

questions.questionText: Which is referred first and best method to find information?
questions.explanation: Textbooks provide foundational knowledge and are often the first resource consulted.

questions.questionText: What is the mechanism of action of NSAIDs?
questions.explanation: NSAIDs primarily work by inhibiting the synthesis of prostaglandins.

questions.questionText: The major adverse effect of long-term corticosteroid use is:
questions.explanation: Long-term use of corticosteroids can lead to osteoporosis.

questions.questionText: Which of the following drugs is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI)?
questions.explanation: Fluoxetine is a well-known SSRI used to treat depression.

questions.questionText: Which route of drug administration is most affected by first pass effect?
questions.explanation: Oral administration is significantly affected by the first pass metabolism in the liver.

questions.questionText: Which drug causes hypokalemia?
questions.explanation: Thiazide diuretics are known to cause hypokalemia.

questions.questionText: The mechanism of action of NSAIDs is:
questions.explanation: NSAIDs (Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs) work primarily by inhibiting cyclooxygenase (COX) enzymes, which are responsible for the production of prostaglandins. By blocking COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes, NSAIDs reduce inflammation, pain, and fever. This mechanism also accounts for their side effects, particularly gastrointestinal issues due to COX-1 inhibition.

questions.questionText: According to the biopharmaceutical classification system (BCS), drug substances having high solubility and low permeability is:
questions.explanation: According to the Biopharmaceutical Classification System (BCS), Class III drugs (not B) have high solubility but low permeability.

questions.questionText: The drug of choice for Wernicke's encephalopathy?
questions.explanation: Thiamin is the drug of choice for treating Wernicke's encephalopathy.

questions.questionText: Which organ is primarily responsible for drug metabolism?
questions.explanation: The liver is the main organ for drug metabolism.

questions.questionText: You were working as a store man pharmacist and want to procure NG tube due to stock. As a pharmacist what should be considered first?
questions.explanation: Size is crucial for ensuring the NG tube fits the patient appropriately.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a macrolide antibiotic?
questions.explanation: Azithromycin is classified as a macrolide antibiotic.

questions.questionText: A 33-year-old patient comes to your hospital for his skin infection, the physician diagnoses HSV and prescribes ketoconazole 2% cream bid for 7 days. After completion of therapy, the patient was not relieved from the infection. What is the most likely problem of this condition?
questions.explanation: The indication is incorrect. Ketoconazole is an antifungal medication which is not effective against HSV (Herpes Simplex Virus), which is a viral infection that requires antiviral medications like acyclovir.

questions.questionText: A major side effect of aminoglycoside antibiotics is:
questions.explanation: Aminoglycosides are known to cause nephrotoxicity.

questions.questionText: The term 'half-life' of a drug refers to:
options: The time required for complete elimination
The time required for the drug concentration to reduce by half
The time taken for drug absorption
questions.explanation: Half-life is defined as the time it takes for the concentration of a drug to reduce to half its initial value.

questions.questionText: Which organ eliminates most drugs from the body?
questions.explanation: The kidneys are the primary organs responsible for drug elimination from the body. While the liver is the main site of drug metabolism (converting drugs into metabolites), it's the kidneys that excrete most drugs and their metabolites through urine, making them the principal route of elimination for most pharmaceutical compounds.

questions.questionText: Which type of drug is used to treat bacterial infections?
questions.explanation: Antibiotics are specifically used to treat bacterial infections.

questions.questionText: Which of the following drug is no refillable schedule - II?
questions.explanation: Methamphetamine is classified as a schedule II drug with no refills.

questions.questionText: A common side effect of ACE inhibitors is:
questions.explanation: Dry cough is a well-known side effect of ACE inhibitors.

questions.questionText: What is the primary function of hemoglobin?
questions.explanation: Hemoglobin's primary function is to transport oxygen in the blood.

questions.questionText: Which class of antibiotics inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis?
questions.explanation: Penicillins inhibit bacterial cell wall synthesis.

questions.questionText: A fresh pharmacist who is doing at the dispensary for the first time gets a prescription that is on read the first letter (D) and the last letter (L). What does he do?
questions.explanation: When a prescription is illegible or unclear, the pharmacist should return it to the prescriber for clarification rather than guessing the medication, which could lead to medication errors. This follows standard pharmacy practice for patient safety.

questions.questionText: Which vitamin is essential for blood clotting?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is crucial for the blood clotting process.

questions.questionText: An established health center wants to start TB treatment for the first time in this health facility. The health center pharmacists have full data about the disease burden frequency of TB clients. Which pharmaceutical quantification method should preferably be used?
questions.explanation: The morbidity method is suitable for quantifying drug needs based on disease burden.

questions.questionText: Which of the following drugs is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI)?
questions.explanation: Omeprazole is a well-known proton pump inhibitor.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a prodrug?
questions.explanation: Enalapril is a prodrug that is converted to its active form in the body.

questions.questionText: A quality control department wants to inspect community pharmacies randomly beyond the inspection program. What type of inspection is done?
questions.explanation: Sudden inspections are unannounced and can occur at any time.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an opioid analgesic?
questions.explanation: Morphine is a classic example of an opioid analgesic.

questions.questionText: What is the normal pH range of blood?
questions.explanation: The normal pH range of blood is between 7.35 and 7.45.

questions.questionText: A pharmacist wants to procure drugs by analyzing VEN. If there is no budget inadequacy, which types of drugs are procured?
questions.explanation: In the VEN (Vital, Essential, Non-essential) analysis, if there is no budget constraint, vital drugs should be procured first as they are life-saving medications and critical to patient care.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true when phenobarbital and warfarin are used together?
questions.explanation: Phenobarbital is a potent enzyme inducer that accelerates the metabolism of warfarin by inducing hepatic cytochrome P450 enzymes. This leads to decreased warfarin plasma levels, reduced anticoagulant effect, and decreased risk of bleeding. This is a clinically significant drug interaction that may require warfarin dose adjustment.

questions.questionText: The pH at which a drug is 50% ionized and 50% unionized is called:
questions.explanation: The pKa (acid dissociation constant) is the pH at which a drug is exactly 50% ionized and 50% unionized. This is an important parameter that influences drug absorption and distribution in the body.

questions.questionText: The pharmacist wants to procure the most costly and most effective drug. Before procurement, what should the pharmacist do?
questions.explanation: Cost effectiveness analysis helps determine the best value for money.

questions.questionText: The drug of choice for anaphylactic shock is:
questions.explanation: Epinephrine is the first-line treatment for anaphylaxis.

questions.questionText: Which analytical method validation parameter is not affected by an increase in the small concentration of the measurement?
questions.explanation: Robustness is a method validation parameter that evaluates the method's capacity to remain unaffected by small deliberate variations in procedural parameters. Unlike linearity, range, and detection limit, robustness is not concentration-dependent but rather measures the reliability of an analytical procedure under different conditions.

questions.questionText: A pharmacist wants to keep drugs on the pallet. What is the appropriate storage of the pallet?
options: At least 20cm away from the wall
At least 20cm away from the floor
At least 30cm away from the wall
At least 1 meter from the floor
questions.explanation: Pallets with pharmaceutical products should be kept at least 20cm away from the floor to prevent moisture damage, facilitate cleaning, and allow proper air circulation. This follows Good Storage Practice (GSP) guidelines for pharmaceutical products.

questions.questionText: What is the main side effect of ACE inhibitors?
questions.explanation: Dry cough is a common side effect of ACE inhibitors.

questions.questionText: What is the primary use of digoxin?
questions.explanation: Digoxin is a cardiac glycoside primarily used to treat heart failure and certain types of cardiac arrhythmias, particularly atrial fibrillation. It increases the strength of heart muscle contractions and slows the heart rate.

questions.questionText: A patient takes antacid and doxycycline. Which of the following food should not be used?
questions.explanation: Dairy products should be avoided when taking doxycycline because the calcium in dairy forms chelates with the antibiotic, significantly reducing its absorption and effectiveness. Additionally, antacids containing calcium, aluminum, or magnesium can also reduce doxycycline absorption and should be taken at least 2 hours apart from the antibiotic.

questions.questionText: Which drug is best for the treatment of emergency asthma?
questions.explanation: Albuterol is a fast-acting bronchodilator used in asthma emergencies.

questions.questionText: What is the main function of insulin in the body?
questions.explanation: Insulin's primary role is to lower blood glucose levels.

questions.questionText: Which class of drugs is used to treat hypertension?
questions.explanation: Beta-blockers are commonly used to manage hypertension.

questions.questionText: A laboratory INR test shows for a patient taking warfarin for his coagulation problem is 12 and there are no bleeding symptoms to the patient. What is the next option?
options: Discontinue warfarin and send to home
Continue warfarin at low dose with INR monitoring
questions.explanation: An INR of 12 is dangerously high (therapeutic range is typically 2-3) and requires immediate intervention even without visible bleeding. The patient is at high risk for spontaneous bleeding. The correct approach is to temporarily discontinue warfarin, consider vitamin K administration if needed, and closely monitor the patient until INR returns to a safer level before resuming therapy at a lower dose.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an anticoagulant?
questions.explanation: Warfarin is a well-known anticoagulant.

questions.questionText: A 65-year-old patient comes to your hospital for medical treatment. The physician diagnoses GERD, which drug should be prescribed?
questions.explanation: Pantoprazole is a proton pump inhibitor effective for GERD.

questions.questionText: A nurse wants reusable medical supply for her routine activities. If she wants to request this supply to pharmacy, which supply may be procured?
questions.explanation: Glass syringes are reusable and can be procured for routine activities.

questions.questionText: The main function of beta-blockers is to:
options: Reduce blood pressure and heart rate
questions.explanation: Beta-blockers primarily reduce blood pressure and heart rate.

questions.questionText: Which vitamin is known as ascorbic acid?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is also known as ascorbic acid.

questions.questionText: Which methods of drug manufacturing is used when the drugs are moisture sensitive and sensitive to high temperature?
questions.explanation: Dry granulation is suitable for moisture-sensitive drugs.

questions.questionText: A physician prescribes an enteric-coated tablet for the treatment of constipation. What is the drug?
questions.explanation: There appears to be an error in this question. Enteric-coated tablets are designed to bypass the stomach and dissolve in the intestine. However, neither amoxicillin nor gentamicin is typically used for constipation. Common enteric-coated medications for GI issues include aspirin, diclofenac, or proton pump inhibitors.

questions.questionText: A client comes to the community pharmacy to buy diclofenac tab for his repeated pain reliever. But the pharmacy refuses the patient to take Paracetamol. Again the patient asks the pharmacy to sell diclofenac and the pharmacy refuses again and sells Paracetamol. Which patient rights are breached?
questions.explanation: This situation breaches the patient's right to dignity and autonomy. The patient has the right to be involved in decisions about their care, including medication choices. While pharmacists should provide professional advice, repeatedly refusing a patient's request without proper explanation or alternatives violates their dignity and right to informed choice.

questions.questionText: What is the main side effect of opioids?
questions.explanation: Constipation is a common side effect of opioid use.

questions.questionText: Which class of drugs is commonly used as anticoagulants?
questions.explanation: Heparins are widely used as anticoagulants.

questions.questionText: A pregnant mother develops Hashimoto's thyroiditis with a normal T4 & T3. Which is the best treatment for this condition?
questions.explanation: In Hashimoto's thyroiditis with normal T3 and T4 levels (subclinical hypothyroidism), levothyroxine is the treatment of choice, especially during pregnancy to prevent adverse effects on fetal development. PTU (propylthiouracil) is used for hyperthyroidism, not hypothyroidism.

questions.questionText: A pharmaceutical analyst wants to test a drug by measuring the absorbance of a drug by analytical instrument. Which of the following analytical instruments is used for this measurement?
questions.explanation: UV spectrophotometers are used to measure absorbance.

questions.questionText: The first-pass effect occurs primarily in the:
questions.explanation: The liver is the primary site for the first-pass metabolism of drugs.

questions.questionText: When to give ASA for ischemic heart disease patients?
questions.explanation: For patients with acute coronary syndrome or ischemic heart disease, aspirin (ASA) should be administered as soon as possible, ideally within 24 hours of symptom onset. Early administration reduces mortality and improves outcomes by preventing further platelet aggregation and thrombus formation.

questions.questionText: Which drug is commonly used in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus?
questions.explanation: Metformin is the first-line treatment for type 2 diabetes.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a broad-spectrum antibiotic?
questions.explanation: Tetracycline is known for its broad-spectrum activity against various bacteria.

questions.questionText: Which drug is used to treat hypothyroidism?
questions.explanation: Levothyroxine is the standard treatment for hypothyroidism.

questions.questionText: The antidote for opioid overdose is:
questions.explanation: Naloxone is the specific antidote for opioid overdose.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a loop diuretic?
questions.explanation: Furosemide is classified as a loop diuretic.

questions.questionText: What is the mechanism of action of beta-lactam antibiotics?
questions.explanation: Beta-lactam antibiotics work by inhibiting the synthesis of bacterial cell walls.

questions.questionText: You are working in the drug manufacturing company and prepare drugs having trace metals and air-sensitive formulation. Which of the following excipient(s) are used to formulate these drugs?
questions.explanation: Chelating agents and antioxidants are used to stabilize sensitive formulations.

questions.questionText: A patient who has PUD does not get relief from Paracetamol for his pain. Which of the following drugs should be prescribed to him?
questions.explanation: For a patient with peptic ulcer disease (PUD), NSAIDs like diclofenac, meloxicam, and indomethacin should be avoided as they can worsen ulcers and increase the risk of GI bleeding. Prednisolone may be considered for specific inflammatory conditions, but it's not typically a first-line pain medication for PUD patients. The most appropriate choice would be an alternative analgesic that doesn't irritate the gastric mucosa.

questions.questionText: Which of the following drug regimen is preferred for a pregnant woman with HIV hepatitis co-infection?
questions.explanation: For pregnant women with HIV and hepatitis co-infection, AZT (zidovudine) + 3TC (lamivudine) + NVP (nevirapine) is preferred. This regimen is effective against both HIV and hepatitis B, has established safety data in pregnancy, and nevirapine has less hepatotoxicity concerns than efavirenz (EFV) in patients with liver disease. TDF (tenofovir) can also be effective but may require careful monitoring for renal function.

questions.questionText: The main neurotransmitter involved in the parasympathetic nervous system is:
questions.explanation: Acetylcholine is the primary neurotransmitter in the parasympathetic nervous system.

questions.questionText: What is the antidote for paracetamol poisoning?
questions.explanation: N-Acetylcysteine is the antidote for paracetamol overdose.

questions.questionText: The primary site of drug metabolism in the body is:
questions.explanation: The liver is the main organ responsible for drug metabolism.

questions.questionText: A patient comes to your hospital for a medical checkup for his hypertension and gout who was on hydrochlorothiazide and prednisolone. Vital signs show that BP is 140/86 mmHg, normal uric acid level, and currently the physician diagnosis shows Cushing's syndrome. Which of the following drugs should not be added to this patient?
questions.explanation: Prednisolone should not be added as the patient is already showing signs of Cushing's syndrome, which is caused by excess corticosteroids. Adding more prednisolone would worsen this condition. Additionally, the patient is already on prednisolone according to the question, so adding more would be inappropriate.

questions.questionText: The primary route of drug excretion is through the:
questions.explanation: The kidneys are the primary organs for drug excretion.

questions.questionText: The mechanism of action of proton pump inhibitors is:
questions.explanation: Proton pump inhibitors inhibit the H⁺/K⁺ ATPase enzyme, reducing gastric acid secretion.

questions.questionText: A quality control company wants to inspect the manufacturing quality of the drug manufacturer. What does the inspector inspect?
questions.explanation: When inspecting drug manufacturing quality, inspectors focus on Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) compliance. GMP encompasses all aspects of production including quality management systems, facility design, equipment validation, production processes, personnel training, and documentation to ensure consistent product quality and safety throughout the manufacturing process.

questions.questionText: For which pharmaceuticals is FEFO strictly used?
questions.explanation: FEFO (First Expired, First Out) is crucial for vaccines to ensure efficacy.

questions.questionText: A patient prescribed to take an antifungal drug for his topical nail infection for 3 months duration. The absorption of this drug is increased by fatty food. Which is the drug?
questions.explanation: Griseofulvin (spelled 'Grisofulvin' in the options) is an antifungal medication used for nail infections whose absorption is significantly increased when taken with fatty foods. It requires a longer duration of therapy (typically 3-6 months for nail infections) and is a classic example of a drug whose bioavailability is enhanced by fatty meals.

questions.questionText: A pharmacist wants to prepare two incompatible active ingredients in one tablet. Which of the following methods are used for this preparation?
questions.explanation: Press coating is used to separate incompatible ingredients in a tablet.

questions.questionText: Which is the most important renal function test?
questions.explanation: Serum creatinine is a key indicator of renal function.

questions.questionText: The therapeutic index of a drug is a measure of:
questions.explanation: The therapeutic index indicates the safety margin of a drug.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an analgesic drug?
questions.explanation: Paracetamol is a widely used analgesic.

questions.questionText: The communication between two pharmacy professionals is:
questions.explanation: Interpersonal communication refers to the exchange of information between two or more individuals. Communication between pharmacy professionals is a form of interpersonal communication as it involves interaction between two separate people.

questions.questionText: What does rheology mean?
questions.explanation: Rheology is the study of the flow and deformation of materials, including all states of matter. It encompasses the flow of liquids (A), deformation of solids (B), and viscosity of liquids (C), making 'All' the correct answer.

questions.questionText: All are the impacts of poor supply chain practice, except:
questions.explanation: Inappropriate selection of medicines is related to formulary decisions and clinical judgment rather than supply chain practices. The other options (stock outs, patient dissatisfaction, and irrational use) can directly result from poor supply chain management.

questions.questionText: Which drug produces effect linearly when the dose is increased?
questions.explanation: Phenobarbitone (phenobarbital) follows zero-order elimination kinetics at higher doses, which results in a linear relationship between dose increases and drug effect. The other listed drugs (triazolam, diazepam, and zolpidem) follow first-order kinetics where the relationship between dose and effect is not linear.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT true about formulary manual?
options: Dosage schedule is basic information in formulary manual.
It is summary information on medicines.
questions.explanation: Formulary manuals are typically not disease-centered but rather focus on medication information.

questions.questionText: The step-wise method of drug information searching is:
questions.explanation: The correct order for drug information searching is from primary to secondary to tertiary sources.

questions.questionText: A patient comes to your Pharmacy with the prescription of Aspirin in small doses (50 to 150 mg per day). What is the most likely reason for prescribing this drug?
options: Is to benefit in patients of unstable angina
May alleviate need for Verapamil in variant angina
questions.explanation: Aspirin at low doses (50-150 mg/day) is commonly prescribed for its antiplatelet effects to prevent cardiovascular events in patients with unstable angina or other cardiovascular conditions. At these low doses, aspirin selectively inhibits cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1) in platelets, reducing thromboxane A2 production and platelet aggregation. It has antithrombotic effects (not thrombolytic, which would dissolve existing clots), and does not replace calcium channel blockers like verapamil in variant angina.

questions.questionText: If you face a patient with absence seizure on valproate and lamotrigine, the most appropriate pharmacy recommendation will be?
questions.explanation: When valproate and lamotrigine are used together, valproate significantly inhibits the metabolism of lamotrigine, increasing lamotrigine levels by approximately 2-fold. Therefore, when adding valproate to a patient already on lamotrigine, the lamotrigine dose should be decreased by about 50% to prevent toxicity. This is a clinically significant drug interaction that requires dose adjustment.

questions.questionText: A 43 years old woman patient who diagnosed with arthritis and amebiasis before 3 months comes to hospital with complaint of weakness, fatigue and muscle spasms. After some lab tests done she has developed megaloblastic anemia and hypoglycemia. From the following drug which one is responsible for hypomagnesemia and vitamin B12 deficiency?
questions.explanation: Omeprazole can lead to vitamin B12 deficiency and hypomagnesemia.

questions.questionText: The characteristics of lyophobic solution is that:
options: Electrolyte in small amount induces stabilization
questions.explanation: All listed characteristics are true for lyophobic solutions.

questions.questionText: A 6-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with a temperature of 104°F (40°C), altered mental status, and petechiae. There is no history of trauma. The results of a toxicology screen are negative. A complete blood cell count reveals 32 × 103 cells/mm3 with 20% bands. Culture results are pending. The patient has no known drug allergies. Which antibiotic regimen provides the best empiric coverage?
questions.explanation: The presentation of high fever, altered mental status, petechiae, and elevated white blood cell count with bandemia strongly suggests meningococcal meningitis or another serious bacterial infection. Ceftriaxone plus vancomycin provides optimal empiric coverage for meningitis, including Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus pneumoniae (including resistant strains), and Haemophilus influenzae until culture results are available.

questions.questionText: Suppose you are working at a hospital & appointed as a secretary in DTC. Which one of the following would NOT be your duty & responsibility?
options: Assessing medicine use to identify problems.
Evaluating and selecting medicines for the formulary list.
Setting regulatory standards for health facilities
questions.explanation: Setting regulatory standards is typically not a responsibility of a DTC secretary.

questions.questionText: To increase the followability of the powder, follow activators are added. From the following which one is referred as follow activators?
questions.explanation: Glidants are used to improve the flow properties of powders.

questions.questionText: Mr. Yilma is a 35-year-old who came to your clinic and treated with ampicillin 500mg qid for 10 days. Six days later, he presents with severe skin rash as a result of ampicillin and you wish to change his medication. Which drug is most likely will not be your preferred option?
questions.explanation: Ceftriaxone would not be the preferred option because it belongs to the cephalosporin class, which may have cross-reactivity with penicillins like ampicillin in patients with penicillin allergy. Approximately 10% of patients with penicillin allergy may also react to cephalosporins.

questions.questionText: A medical supply used for healing and preventing infection of wounds, burns, and ulcers are:
questions.explanation: Surgical dressings are specifically designed for wound care.

questions.questionText: In patients infected with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), which of the following symptoms is/are likely to be the clinical stage three manifestation of being infected?
questions.explanation: Pulmonary Tuberculosis is a common stage three manifestation in HIV patients.

questions.questionText: What type of medical equipment are medical imaging machines such as X-ray, CT scan and MRI scan?
questions.explanation: Medical imaging machines are classified as diagnostic equipment.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the primary long-term controller medication for a 5-year-old female with moderate persistent asthma?
questions.explanation: Fluticasone propionate is a first-line controller medication for asthma.

questions.questionText: The requisition of medicines by different dispensary from the pharmacy store should be carried out using:
options: Internal Facility Reporting and Requisition Form (IFRR)
questions.explanation: The IFRR is typically used for requisitioning medicines.

questions.questionText: Which resource do you use to check for the safety of medications during pregnancy?
questions.explanation: All types of resources can provide information on medication safety during pregnancy.

title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Pharmacy (2015)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Pharmacy (2015). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: The communication between two pharmacy professionals is:
questions.explanation: Interpersonal communication refers to the exchange of information between two or more individuals. Communication between pharmacy professionals is a form of interpersonal communication as it involves interaction between two separate people.

questions.questionText: What does rheology mean?
questions.explanation: Rheology is the study of the flow and deformation of materials, including all states of matter. It encompasses the flow of liquids (A), deformation of solids (B), and viscosity of liquids (C), making 'All' the correct answer.

questions.questionText: All are the impacts of poor supply chain practice, except:
questions.explanation: Inappropriate selection of medicines is related to formulary decisions and clinical judgment rather than supply chain practices. The other options (stock outs, patient dissatisfaction, and irrational use) can directly result from poor supply chain management.

questions.questionText: Which drug produces effect linearly when the dose is increased?
questions.explanation: Phenobarbitone (phenobarbital) follows zero-order elimination kinetics at higher doses, which results in a linear relationship between dose increases and drug effect. The other listed drugs (triazolam, diazepam, and zolpidem) follow first-order kinetics where the relationship between dose and effect is not linear.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT true about formulary manual?
options: Dosage schedule is basic information in formulary manual.
It is summary information on medicines.
questions.explanation: Formulary manuals are typically not disease-centered but rather focus on medication information.

questions.questionText: The step-wise method of drug information searching is:
questions.explanation: The correct order for drug information searching is from primary to secondary to tertiary sources.

questions.questionText: A patient comes to your Pharmacy with the prescription of Aspirin in small doses (50 to 150 mg per day). What is the most likely reason for prescribing this drug?
options: Is to benefit in patients of unstable angina
May alleviate need for Verapamil in variant angina
questions.explanation: Aspirin at low doses (50-150 mg/day) is commonly prescribed for its antiplatelet effects to prevent cardiovascular events in patients with unstable angina or other cardiovascular conditions. At these low doses, aspirin selectively inhibits cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1) in platelets, reducing thromboxane A2 production and platelet aggregation. It has antithrombotic effects (not thrombolytic, which would dissolve existing clots), and does not replace calcium channel blockers like verapamil in variant angina.

questions.questionText: If you face a patient with absence seizure on valproate and lamotrigine, the most appropriate pharmacy recommendation will be?
questions.explanation: When valproate and lamotrigine are used together, valproate significantly inhibits the metabolism of lamotrigine, increasing lamotrigine levels by approximately 2-fold. Therefore, when adding valproate to a patient already on lamotrigine, the lamotrigine dose should be decreased by about 50% to prevent toxicity. This is a clinically significant drug interaction that requires dose adjustment.

questions.questionText: A 43 years old woman patient who diagnosed with arthritis and amebiasis before 3 months comes to hospital with complaint of weakness, fatigue and muscle spasms. After some lab tests done she has developed megaloblastic anemia and hypoglycemia. From the following drug which one is responsible for hypomagnesemia and vitamin B12 deficiency?
questions.explanation: Omeprazole can lead to vitamin B12 deficiency and hypomagnesemia.

questions.questionText: The characteristics of lyophobic solution is that:
options: Electrolyte in small amount induces stabilization
questions.explanation: All listed characteristics are true for lyophobic solutions.

questions.questionText: A 6-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with a temperature of 104°F (40°C), altered mental status, and petechiae. There is no history of trauma. The results of a toxicology screen are negative. A complete blood cell count reveals 32 × 103 cells/mm3 with 20% bands. Culture results are pending. The patient has no known drug allergies. Which antibiotic regimen provides the best empiric coverage?
questions.explanation: The presentation of high fever, altered mental status, petechiae, and elevated white blood cell count with bandemia strongly suggests meningococcal meningitis or another serious bacterial infection. Ceftriaxone plus vancomycin provides optimal empiric coverage for meningitis, including Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus pneumoniae (including resistant strains), and Haemophilus influenzae until culture results are available.

questions.questionText: Suppose you are working at a hospital & appointed as a secretary in DTC. Which one of the following would NOT be your duty & responsibility?
options: Assessing medicine use to identify problems.
Evaluating and selecting medicines for the formulary list.
Setting regulatory standards for health facilities
questions.explanation: Setting regulatory standards is typically not a responsibility of a DTC secretary.

questions.questionText: To increase the followability of the powder, follow activators are added. From the following which one is referred as follow activators?
questions.explanation: Glidants are used to improve the flow properties of powders.

questions.questionText: Mr. Yilma is a 35-year-old who came to your clinic and treated with ampicillin 500mg qid for 10 days. Six days later, he presents with severe skin rash as a result of ampicillin and you wish to change his medication. Which drug is most likely will not be your preferred option?
questions.explanation: Ceftriaxone would not be the preferred option because it belongs to the cephalosporin class, which may have cross-reactivity with penicillins like ampicillin in patients with penicillin allergy. Approximately 10% of patients with penicillin allergy may also react to cephalosporins.

questions.questionText: A medical supply used for healing and preventing infection of wounds, burns, and ulcers are:
questions.explanation: Surgical dressings are specifically designed for wound care.

questions.questionText: In patients infected with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), which of the following symptoms is/are likely to be the clinical stage three manifestation of being infected?
questions.explanation: Pulmonary Tuberculosis is a common stage three manifestation in HIV patients.

questions.questionText: What type of medical equipment are medical imaging machines such as X-ray, CT scan and MRI scan?
questions.explanation: Medical imaging machines are classified as diagnostic equipment.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the primary long-term controller medication for a 5-year-old female with moderate persistent asthma?
questions.explanation: Fluticasone propionate is a first-line controller medication for asthma.

questions.questionText: The requisition of medicines by different dispensary from the pharmacy store should be carried out using:
options: Internal Facility Reporting and Requisition Form (IFRR)
questions.explanation: The IFRR is typically used for requisitioning medicines.

questions.questionText: Which resource do you use to check for the safety of medications during pregnancy?
questions.explanation: All types of resources can provide information on medication safety during pregnancy.

questions.questionText: Choline esters like carbachol are most likely to cause which of the following adverse effects?
questions.explanation: Choline esters such as carbachol are cholinergic agonists that stimulate muscarinic receptors, causing parasympathetic effects summarized by the mnemonic SLUDGE: Salivation, Lacrimation, Urination, Defecation, GI distress, and Emesis. Salivation is a characteristic muscarinic effect, while anhydrosis (option A) and tachycardia (option D) are anticholinergic effects. Delirium (option B) is typically associated with anticholinergic activity, not cholinergic stimulation.

questions.questionText: T.R is 40 years old farmers taking hydrocodone 60mg po BID for pain management. If the equivalent dose of hydrocodone and hydromorphone is 30mg and 7.5mg, respectively. What will be daily dose of hydromorphone that you recommend for T.R if hydrocodone is stock out?
questions.explanation: To convert from hydrocodone to hydromorphone: The patient takes 60mg hydrocodone BID = 120mg/day. The conversion ratio is 30mg hydrocodone = 7.5mg hydromorphone. Therefore, 120mg hydrocodone ÷ 30mg × 7.5mg = 30mg hydromorphone daily.

questions.questionText: Nonverbal communication involves _________ to generate meaning.
questions.explanation: Nonverbal communication primarily involves the use of symbols.

questions.questionText: K.E. is a 29-year-old asymptomatic patient who is HIV positive. She recently found out she is pregnant and is estimated to be early in her first trimester. Her most recent CD4 count was 170 cells/mm3, and her viral load was 100,000 copies/mL by reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction. Which is the best therapy for K.E. to prevent HIV transmission to her child?
options: No drug therapy is needed; the risks to the fetus outweigh any benefits.
Administer zidovudine 300 mg twice daily orally throughout the pregnancy, followed by zidovudine during labor and consequently to the infant for 6 weeks.
No drug therapy is needed now, but administer a single dose of nevirapine at the onset of labor.
Administer a potent combination antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimen.
questions.explanation: For an HIV-positive pregnant woman with a low CD4 count (170 cells/mm3) and high viral load (100,000 copies/mL), a potent combination antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimen is the standard of care. This approach is most effective at reducing maternal viral load and preventing mother-to-child transmission.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about volatile oils?
options: Most of them are optically inactive
Consist of glyceryl esters of fatty acids
They leave a permanent grease spot on paper and cannot be saponified with alkalies
questions.explanation: Volatile oils leave a grease spot and are not saponifiable.

questions.questionText: Not true for zero order kinetics of drug elimination?
options: Constant amount of drug eliminated per unit time
Ethanol and aspirin follow zero order kinetics
Rate of elimination affected by concentration
Toxicity is mainly suspected for drug eliminated by this order of kinetics
questions.explanation: In zero-order kinetics, the rate of elimination is constant and NOT affected by the drug concentration. This is the key distinction from first-order kinetics, where elimination rate is proportional to concentration. Zero-order kinetics typically occurs when elimination pathways become saturated, as with ethanol and high-dose aspirin, and this property increases risk of toxicity since elimination doesn't accelerate with increasing concentrations.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is false about the properties of tannins?
options: Cause agglutination of red blood cells
questions.explanation: Tannins are generally NOT soluble in organic solvents (option B is false). They are water-soluble polyphenolic compounds that are acidic in nature, typically non-crystallizable, and can cause protein precipitation including the agglutination of red blood cells due to their ability to bind with proteins.

questions.questionText: Probenecid is effective in treating gout because it decreases which of the following?
questions.explanation: Probenecid decreases the reabsorption of uric acid in the kidneys.

questions.questionText: An example for colloidal system is:
questions.explanation: Suspensions and emulsions are examples of colloidal systems.

questions.questionText: __ is the ability of an analytical method to be unaffected by small, deliberate changes in operating parameters.
questions.explanation: Robustness refers to the method's ability to remain unaffected by small changes.

questions.questionText: M.N is a 38 years old female with absence seizure with history of epidermal necrosis last year. Your recommendation should exclude one of the following drug for M.N?
questions.explanation: Lamotrigine is associated with a risk of serious skin reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis. The patient's history of epidermal necrosis means lamotrigine should be avoided. Ethosuximide does not typically cause these reactions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following are the recommended blood pressure and lipid goals for the prevention of cardiovascular disease in adults with diabetes?
questions.explanation: The recommended goals for diabetic patients according to the American Diabetes Association for cardiovascular disease prevention are: blood pressure less than 130/80 mmHg, triglycerides less than 150 mg/dL, and LDL cholesterol less than 100 mg/dL (option D).

questions.questionText: A condition/phenomena, where the added molecules are partitioned in favor of the interface/surface, is:
questions.explanation: Adsorption refers to the accumulation of molecules at the surface/interface.

questions.questionText: Which of the following asthma therapies has been shown to result in reduced death and hospitalizations for patients with asthma?
questions.explanation: Inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) are proven to reduce mortality and hospitalizations in asthma patients.

questions.questionText: JT. is a 62-year-old man with a history of CHD (MI 3 years ago), HTN, depression, chronic kidney disease (CKD). Her medication includes enalapril 10mg daily, metoprolol 50mg twice daily, aspirin 81mg daily and amitriptyline 100mg daily. From her current medication one may increase risk of arrhythmia?
questions.explanation: Amitriptyline, a tricyclic antidepressant, can increase the risk of arrhythmias, especially in patients with existing cardiac conditions and CKD. TCAs have quinidine-like effects that can prolong the QT interval and cause conduction abnormalities. This risk is heightened in patients with cardiac disease and impaired renal function.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a recommended antibiotic choice for a patient who is in need of long-term antibiotic prophylaxis against spontaneous bacterial peritonitis?
questions.explanation: Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim is commonly used for prophylaxis against spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.

questions.questionText: Homogenous mixture prepared by dissolving a solid, liquid, gas or group of preparations in a given solvent is:
questions.explanation: A solution is a homogeneous mixture of solute and solvent.

questions.questionText: A 42-year-old woman is noted to have Type II diabetes for 20 years. She is noted to have hypertension with BP in the 150/94 range. The urinalysis shows mild proteinuria. Which of the following drugs would be the best to treat the hypertension in this individual?
questions.explanation: Enalapril is preferred for treating hypertension in diabetic patients with proteinuria.

questions.questionText: An infant born at 36 weeks' gestation develops respiratory distress, hypotension, and mottling at 5 hours of life. The child is transported to the neonatal intensive care unit, where he has a witnessed seizure, and cultures are obtained. Maternal vaginal cultures are positive for group B Streptococcus, and three doses of penicillin were given to the mother before delivery. Which is the best empiric antibiotic regimen?
questions.explanation: Vancomycin plus cefotaxime is the preferred regimen in this case. With maternal GBS colonization despite penicillin prophylaxis, the infant may have a resistant strain. Vancomycin provides coverage for resistant GBS, while cefotaxime covers gram-negative pathogens and crosses the blood-brain barrier (important due to the seizure). Additionally, ceftriaxone is typically avoided in neonates due to risk of kernicterus.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is used to measure the blood oxygen level and pulse rate?
questions.explanation: An oximeter is used to measure blood oxygen levels and pulse rates.

questions.questionText: A 16-year-old male is having an acute asthmatic attack. Epinephrine is given via SC route. Which of the following best describes the cellular action of epinephrine?
options: Decreased activity of cAMP-dependent protein kinases
Inhibition of the activity of phospholipase
questions.explanation: Epinephrine activates adenylyl cyclase, increasing cAMP levels.

questions.questionText: Minimum standard area for compounding room according to Ethiopian guideline is:
options: 25 m square size with shortest side not less than 9 m
9 m square size with shortest side not less than 2.5 m
25 m square size with shortest side not less than 4 m
16 m square size with shortest side not less than 3 m
questions.explanation: The minimum standard area for a compounding room is 25 m² with specific dimensions.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not tells about pharmacokinetics?
options: Alkalization of urine facilitates the excretion of acidic drug
Drug dose adjustment is necessary in Kidney insufficiency patient
Most drug response is due to their interaction with receptor
Plasma protein affects the distribution of drugs
questions.explanation: While drug response is influenced by receptor interaction, pharmacokinetics focuses on drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion.

questions.questionText: R.M is a 30 years old woman of 36 weeks of gestation age presented with preeclampsia to her primary clinic. She evaluated for preeclampsia and prescribed magnesium sulfate. One of the following drug used for management of magnesium sulfate toxicity in R.M as antidote:
questions.explanation: Calcium gluconate is the antidote for magnesium sulfate toxicity.

questions.questionText: A 5-month-old infant who was born at term and is otherwise healthy was treated for her first case of otitis media with amoxicillin 45 mg/kg/day for 7 days. On follow-up examination, her pediatrician noticed fullness in the middle ear and a cloudy tympanic membrane with decreased mobility. She is now afebrile and eating well. Which is the best recommendation for her treatment?
options: Decongestant and antihistamine daily until resolution.
questions.explanation: High-dose amoxicillin is recommended for persistent otitis media.

questions.questionText: Newton's law of Viscosity states that:
options: Shearing stress and rate of shear are directly proportional.
Shearing stress and rate of shear are inversely proportional.
Shearing stress and rate of shear are independent of each other.
Shearing stress is the square root of rate shear.
questions.explanation: Newton's law of viscosity states that the shearing stress (τ) is directly proportional to the rate of shear (γ), expressed as τ = η × γ, where η is the coefficient of viscosity. This relationship defines Newtonian fluids, where viscosity remains constant regardless of the applied shear rate or shear stress.

questions.questionText: A 38-year-old man presents to the clinic complaining of leg swelling. He has a long history of hypertension and diabetes, with a recent change in his medications, although he cannot remember the names of the new drugs. He has no other complaints, and he denies any shortness of breath or orthopnea. His physical examination, other than bilateral edema of the lower extremities, is completely normal. Which medication is most likely responsible for the patient's complaint?
questions.explanation: Amlodipine is known to cause peripheral edema as a side effect.

questions.questionText: P.E. is a 56-year-old man who comes to the clinic with a 3-day history of fever, chills, pleuritic chest pain, malaise, and productive cough. In the clinic, his temperature is 102.1°F (38.9°C) (all other vital signs are normal). His chest radiograph reveals consolidation in the right lower lobe. His white blood cell count (WBC) is 14,400 cells/mm3, but all other laboratory values are normal. He is given a diagnosis of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). He has not received any antibiotics in 5 years and has no chronic disease states. Which is the best empiric therapy for P.E.?
options: Cefuroxime axetil 250 mg orally twice daily.
Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole double strength orally twice daily.
questions.explanation: Levofloxacin 750 mg daily is an appropriate empiric therapy for community-acquired pneumonia in adults with no comorbidities. It provides coverage against common CAP pathogens including Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and atypical organisms. Guidelines recommend respiratory fluoroquinolones as one of the first-line options for outpatient treatment of CAP.

questions.questionText: A patient who develops hypersensitivity previously to this drug should never be re-challenged in future plan of antiretroviral therapy?
questions.explanation: Abacavir can cause a potentially life-threatening hypersensitivity reaction (HSR) in patients with the HLA-B*5701 allele. Re-exposure to abacavir after a hypersensitivity reaction can result in a rapid, severe, and potentially fatal reaction. Therefore, abacavir should never be reintroduced in patients with a history of hypersensitivity, regardless of HLA status.
