questions.questionText: What scattering mechanism, according to the Drude model, limits the motion of free electrons in a metal?
options: Collisions with phonons (vibrations of the metal lattice)
questions.explanation: Collisions with phonons limit the motion of free electrons in metals according to the Drude model.

questions.questionText: In a face-centered cubic (FCC) unit cell, how many atoms are located on corners?
questions.explanation: In an FCC unit cell, there are 8 corner atoms, each contributing 1/8 to the unit cell, totaling 1 atom.

questions.questionText: The electrical conductivity of a metal is primarily due to:
options: The strong attraction between electrons and nuclei
The motion of free electrons under an applied electric field
The fixed positions of the atomic cores
questions.explanation: The motion of free electrons under an electric field is the primary reason for electrical conductivity in metals.

questions.questionText: What is the coordination number of simple cubic structure?
questions.explanation: The coordination number of a simple cubic structure is 6, as each atom is surrounded by 6 nearest neighbors.

questions.questionText: In a semiconductor, the Fermi level (EF) lies:
options: Always at the bottom of the conduction band.
Always at the top of the valence band.
Within the bandgap or at the band edges, depending on doping.
Cannot be determined without material information.
questions.explanation: The Fermi level in a semiconductor can lie within the bandgap or at the band edges based on doping.

questions.questionText: The Fermi energy (EF) in a metal represents:
options: The energy required to remove an electron from the metal.
The average kinetic energy of the electrons.
The maximum energy level that an electron can occupy at absolute zero temperature.
The energy difference between the highest and lowest occupied energy levels.
questions.explanation: The Fermi energy represents the maximum energy level occupied by electrons at absolute zero.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is equivalent to the Miller indices (211)?
questions.explanation: The equivalent Miller indices for (211) can be expressed as (ˉ21ˉ1).

questions.questionText: The phenomenon where a piezoelectric material generates a voltage when subjected to mechanical stress is called:
questions.explanation: The piezoelectric effect describes the generation of voltage in response to mechanical stress.

questions.questionText: Which of the following elements is most likely to form a metallic bond?
questions.explanation: Sodium (Na) is a metal and is most likely to form metallic bonds.

questions.questionText: The Fermi energy (E_F) represents:
options: The average energy of all electrons in the metal
The energy required to remove an electron from the metal
The highest occupied energy level at absolute zero temperature
The energy difference between the highest and lowest energy levels
questions.explanation: The Fermi energy represents the highest occupied energy level at absolute zero temperature.

questions.questionText: The permittivity (ε) of a material is related to the permittivity of free space (ε₀) and the dielectric constant (κ) by the equation:
questions.explanation: The permittivity of a material is given by ε = ε₀ κ.

title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Plant Science (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Plant Science (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: Plant Hormone is a naturally-occurring compound which regulates change in physiology, growth or development of the plant. Among the following which one is responsible to control dwarfness of the plant?
questions.explanation: Gibberellins (GA) are responsible for controlling dwarfness in plants.

questions.questionText: Plant cell type which are alive at maturity and have only a primary wall; provide mechanical support during growth?
questions.explanation: Collenchyma cells are living at maturity, have primary walls with uneven thickenings rich in pectin and hemicellulose, and provide mechanical support to growing plant parts. Sclerenchyma cells are typically dead at maturity with thick secondary walls, while parenchyma cells are thin-walled and serve for storage and metabolism rather than primary mechanical support.

questions.questionText: A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more components in which the particle size is smaller than 1 nm. In which type of solutions the cell shrinks when it is placed in this solution?
questions.explanation: In hypertonic solutions, water moves out of the cell causing it to shrink.

questions.questionText: The minerals absorbed by the roots are mineral ions dissolved in the soil and water. They support plants to complete their life cycle and are to produce seeds. Which of the following is present in the green pigment of the leaf?
questions.explanation: Magnesium (Mg) is a central component of chlorophyll, the green pigment in leaves.

questions.questionText: The rate at which water moves through the plants due to transpiration plays an important role in maintaining plant water balance. Which of the following is the instrument for measuring the rate of transpiration in plants?
questions.explanation: A potometer is used to measure the rate of water uptake (transpiration) in plants.

questions.questionText: Food preservation can be defined as the process of treating and handling food in such a way as to stop or greatly slow down spoilage and prevent foodborne illness while maintaining nutritional value, texture and flavor. Why is low temperature maintained for preservation?
questions.explanation: Low temperatures slow down bacterial growth, minimizing spoilage.

questions.questionText: What is an example of positive geotropism in plants?
questions.explanation: Positive geotropism (or gravitropism) is growth toward gravity, demonstrated by roots growing downward. Stems growing upward exhibit negative geotropism, lateral root growth is diagravitropism, and flower closing is a thigmotropic or nyctinastic response, not primarily gravitropic.

questions.questionText: As you will be a plant Agronomist in commercial crop farms and the area is characterized by erratic rainfall you need to plan to get high production within drought situation, what is your plan to achieve the above goal?
options: Maintaining water balance by irrigation supplements
questions.explanation: All options are valid strategies for managing drought conditions.

questions.questionText: Simultaneous fusion of the generative nuclei one with egg cell and other with the endospermic nuclei is termed?
questions.explanation: Double fertilization is unique to angiosperms where one sperm fertilizes the egg and another fertilizes the endosperm.

questions.questionText: The Rudimentary root of the seed or seedling that forms the primary root of the young plant is called as?
questions.explanation: The radicle is the embryonic root that develops into the primary root.

questions.questionText: Seed is botanically called as?
questions.explanation: Botanically, a seed is a ripened ovule containing an embryo.

questions.questionText: The process of Seed drying is very important to maintain its?
questions.explanation: Proper seed drying is crucial for maintaining seed viability (ability to germinate) and vigor (strength and rate of germination). Excessive moisture in seeds accelerates deterioration through increased respiration, enzyme activity, and pathogen growth. Controlled drying to appropriate moisture content (typically 8-12% depending on species) extends storage life while preserving germination potential.

questions.questionText: A sound seed certification programme requires?
questions.explanation: Seed certification programs require legal frameworks (seed laws) to ensure quality standards.

questions.questionText: Free from inert matter and defective seeds are termed as?
questions.explanation: Physical purity refers to seeds free from inert matter and defective seeds.

questions.questionText: Possible reasons for seed dormancy is/are?
questions.explanation: All listed factors can contribute to seed dormancy.

questions.questionText: As you will be a Seed science expert in commercial fruit farms and you need to prepare seedlings form dormant seeds to your production site, what you will do?
questions.explanation: All methods (scarification, light treatment, stratification) can break seed dormancy.

questions.questionText: Primitive cultivars cultivated by farmers over generation and generation is known as?
questions.explanation: Land races are traditional varieties developed through generations of farmer selection.

questions.questionText: Single, Self-pollinated, homozygous plant is called as?
questions.explanation: A pure line is a homozygous, self-pollinated plant variety.

questions.questionText: Within an agricultural context drought is a prolonged period of deficit precipitation which results in negative impact on crop growth or yield. Among the following which one is the type of chemical which is accumulated when plants are under drought conditions?
questions.explanation: Proline is an amino acid that accumulates as an osmoprotectant during drought stress. It helps maintain cell turgor, stabilize proteins and cellular structures, and scavenge reactive oxygen species. Other compatible solutes that may accumulate during drought include glycine betaine and sugars. Plant hormones like abscisic acid also increase, while growth hormones like gibberellins, auxins, and cytokinins typically decrease during drought stress.

questions.questionText: Genetic Variation in clones may arise due to?
questions.explanation: All factors can introduce genetic variation in clones.

questions.questionText: Breeding for disease resistance requires
questions.explanation: All elements are necessary for successful disease resistance breeding.

questions.questionText: During hybridization how we can remove stamens from the flower bud?
questions.explanation: Emasculation is the removal of stamens to prevent self-pollination.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not used for crop improvement?
questions.explanation: Mutations are actually widely used for crop improvement. Natural and induced mutations create genetic variation that can be selected for desirable traits. The correct answer might have been intended to be something else, but all listed options are valid crop improvement methods.

questions.questionText: If water table is comparatively high, the irrigation canal becomes useless, due to?
options: Water logging of the cultivated areas
questions.explanation: High water tables cause multiple irrigation problems.

questions.questionText: The main cause of silting up a channel is?
questions.explanation: All factors contribute to channel silting.

questions.questionText: Pick up the correct statement from the following?
options: Gravity water is harmful to crops
Hygroscopic water remains attached to soil molecules by chemical bond
Capillary moisture held in the soil pores against gravity by surface tension, is utilized by plants
questions.explanation: Capillary water is available for plant uptake.

questions.questionText: Pick up the incorrect statement from the following?
options: In free flooding irrigation, water is admitted at one corner of a field and is allowed to spread over the entire area
In check method of irrigation, the field is divided into smaller compartments and water is admitted to each in turn
In furrow irrigation water is admitted between the rows of plants in the field
questions.explanation: All statements about irrigation methods are correct.

questions.questionText: A fall in a canal bed is generally provided, if
options: Ground slope exceeds the designed bed slope
Designed bed slope exceeds the ground slope
Ground slope is practically the same as the designed bed slope
questions.explanation: Falls are needed when ground slope exceeds designed slope to control water velocity.

questions.questionText: Effective precipitation for a crop may be defined as?
options: Total precipitation minus the loss due to evaporation
Total precipitation minus the loss due to infiltration
Total precipitation during the crop period
Available water stored in soil within root zone of the crop
questions.explanation: Effective precipitation is the water actually available to crops in the root zone.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: The canal system and the drainage system are complementary
The canal system runs on ridges, gets divided into smaller channels and spreads its water on the land
The drainage system runs along the lowest line, collects drainage water from the slopes and joins the main stream
questions.explanation: All statements about irrigation and drainage systems are correct.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the chemical which is used for killing unwanted weeds?
questions.explanation: Herbicides are specifically designed to control weeds.

questions.questionText: Of the following, which one is false about weeds?
options: Weeds are pests and guest plants
Parasitic weeds are independent on the soils to grow
All weeds have no beneficial effect for other
questions.explanation: Some weeds can have beneficial effects, such as providing habitat for beneficial insects, preventing soil erosion, contributing organic matter to soil, or having medicinal properties. Many weeds that are considered 'nuisance plants' in one context may have ecological or economic value in other contexts.

questions.questionText: Biology of weeds which deals about?
options: The interaction between weeds and their environment
The classification of weeds based on their origin
questions.explanation: Weed biology focuses on weed-environment interactions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the method of classifying weeds morphologically?
options: Based on the impact of the environmental effects of the animals
Based on plant structure (e.g., grasses vs broadleaves)
questions.explanation: Morphological classification is based on physical characteristics.

questions.questionText: Of the following, which one is not encourage the establishment and survival of weeds?
questions.explanation: Good agronomic practices suppress weeds.

questions.questionText: Inhibition of a plant's growth due to the release of bio-chemicals in the environment is?
questions.explanation: Allelopathy involves biochemical inhibition of plant growth.

questions.questionText: The minimum period of time during which the crop must be free of weeds in order to prevent loss in yield is?
questions.explanation: This critical period determines when weed control is most crucial.

questions.questionText: Which one is not true about modern tillage?
questions.explanation: 'Many tillage' is not a recognized modern tillage practice.

questions.questionText: Crops grown and plowed under while still green in order to improve soil fertility is?
questions.explanation: Green manure crops are incorporated to enrich soil fertility.

questions.questionText: Ability of seeds to germinate under optimal conditions is?
questions.explanation: Viability refers to seed germination potential.

questions.questionText: All of the following crops are two seasonal, except one?
questions.explanation: Wheat is typically a single-season crop.

questions.questionText: Of the following statements, which one is not true about pulse crops?
options: Their seeds are rich in protein
questions.explanation: Pulse crops typically exhibit epigeal germination, where the cotyledons emerge above ground (not hypogeal where cotyledons remain below ground). Examples like beans, chickpeas, and lentils demonstrate epigeal germination, making the statement 'They are hypogal during germination' false.

questions.questionText: An irreversible increase in size, volume or mass of a cell or organ or whole organisms?
questions.explanation: Growth is defined as irreversible increase in size/mass.

questions.questionText: Of the following, which one is not major cereal crop of Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Soybean is a legume, not a cereal crop.

questions.questionText: Which experimental design involves main plots and sub-plots in its layout?
questions.explanation: Split plot designs have nested treatments (main plots and subplots).

questions.questionText: One of the following is not source of variation of RCBD?
questions.explanation: Columns aren't a standard source of variation in RCBD.

questions.questionText: Which of the following experimental design is most widely used in field?
questions.explanation: RCBD is most common for field experiments due to blocking.

questions.questionText: What is the value of an 'A' in the ANOVA table?
questions.explanation: In the ANOVA table, 'A' represents the Error Sum of Squares, calculated as Total SS - (Block SS + Treatment SS) = 30.45 - (15 + 10) = 5.45.

questions.questionText: Calculated value of 'D' is?
questions.explanation: Error DF = Total DF - (Block DF + Treatment DF) = 15 - (3 + 3) = 9.

questions.questionText: Which one is the calculated value of F?
questions.explanation: F = Treatment MS / Error MS = (10/3)/(5.45/9) ≈ 3.33.

questions.questionText: What the least significant difference (LSD) of the study?
questions.explanation: The LSD is calculated using the formula: LSD = t(α/2, df) × √(2 × MSE/r), where t is the critical t-value, MSE is the mean square error, and r is the number of replications. Given the information available, 1.24 is the correct LSD value.

questions.questionText: Of the following which one is true?
options: High temperature increase the rate of water loss in vegetable crops
Vegetable products must be stored at high RH (>90%) except: root and tuber crops (RH=50 - 60%)
The temperature at which maximum storage is attained varies from product to product
questions.explanation: All statements about vegetable storage are correct.

questions.questionText: A science dealing with cultivation, harvesting, post-harvest handling, processing and marketing of vegetable crops?
questions.explanation: Olericulture is the science of vegetable production.

questions.questionText: Which vegetables are growing under the ground?
questions.explanation: Root/tuber crops grow underground.

questions.questionText: Of the following which one is the importance of vegetables storage?
options: To ensure regular supply of seasonal produce all year round
Preservation of nutritional quality and weapon for national stability
questions.explanation: All options describe benefits of vegetable storage.

questions.questionText: As you will be a plant science production expert in commercial vegetable farms and you need to prepare seedlings for your production site, what is your consideration for vegetable nursery site selection?
questions.explanation: Soil quality and water availability are critical for nurseries.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: All matches are actually correct: Sweet potato is a root crop (modified storage roots), Tomato is botanically a fruit vegetable, Onion is a bulb crop, and Cabbage is a leafy vegetable. The question may have been intended to ask which is 'incorrectly' matched, but as written, all options are valid classifications.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the opportunities for vegetables production in Ethiopia?
options: The presence of favorable agro-ecological conditions for successful growing of various fruit crops
Proximity of the country to fertile markets of Europe and Middle East Asia
questions.explanation: All factors present opportunities for Ethiopian vegetable production.

questions.questionText: Which method of classification is very helpful for botanist and breeder who are interested to study morphology, cross ability and taxonomic character?
options: Classification based on nature and structure of ovary wall
questions.explanation: Botanical classification is most useful for taxonomic studies.

questions.questionText: Banana is commercially propagated by?
questions.explanation: Sword suckers are the preferred banana propagation material.

questions.questionText: Among the following which one is a post-harvest practice accomplished by flooding spraying or immersing the produce by water?
questions.explanation: Hydrocooling uses water immersion for rapid cooling.

questions.questionText: Which is not applicable to vegetatively propagated fruits?
options: To get true to type plants
To get a new type of plant
questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation maintains existing genotypes, doesn't create new ones.

questions.questionText: Of the following which one is pre-condition required for establishment of orchards?
questions.explanation: All steps are necessary for orchard establishment.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: All climate-fruit pairings are correct.

questions.questionText: As you will be a plant science production manager in large scale fruit farm and you need to expand the area of production site, what is your consideration for that purpose?
questions.explanation: All factors (temperature, soil, water availability, and market access) are critical considerations for orchard expansion. Market access is particularly important for commercial viability, but a comprehensive approach would consider all these factors together for successful expansion.

questions.questionText: Which one is an approach for searching new facts through organized scientific investigation?
questions.explanation: Research is systematic investigation to discover new knowledge.

questions.questionText: Which one the following is a purpose of a research?
options: to provide solution for complex problems
questions.explanation: Both problem-solving and hypothesis testing are research purposes.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following terms well define qualitative data?
questions.explanation: Qualitative data is characterized by being non-numerical, descriptive, and often used in anthropological and sociological research. It includes observations that can be described but not precisely measured numerically. Options B and C both describe aspects of qualitative data, making 'All except A' the correct comprehensive answer.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct steps for scientific research?
options: problem identification- analysis- data collection- reviewing information
drawing conclusion – analysis – data collection – problem identification
problem identification – reviewing information – data collection – analysis – drawing conclusion
questions.explanation: This sequence represents the standard scientific method.

questions.questionText: The written document for the requesting both authorization and funds to undertake a specific project in a laboratory, library or field is called?
questions.explanation: A research proposal seeks approval and funding.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not an outline of research proposal?
questions.explanation: Results come after proposal approval, not in the proposal itself.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an assumption or guesses about the relationship between two research variable?
questions.explanation: A hypothesis predicts relationships between variables.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an abiotic factor for the development of a plant disease?
questions.explanation: Weather is a non-living (abiotic) disease factor.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a symptom of diseased plant?
questions.explanation: All options describe plant disease symptoms.

questions.questionText: One of the following is the scanting pattern of disease assessment in the field?
questions.explanation: All patterns are used for field disease assessment.

questions.questionText: Among the following which one is an organism that man regards as a harmful to his personal properties or environment?
questions.explanation: Pests are organisms harmful to human interests.

questions.questionText: Of the following one is defined as the physical harm or distraction to a valued commodity caused by the presence of activity of a pest?
questions.explanation: Damage refers to actual harm caused by pests.

questions.questionText: Which of the following are the major pillars of disease triangle?
options: Resistant Host- a virulent pathogen – none conducting environment
Susceptible Host – virulent pathogen – conducive environment
questions.explanation: Disease requires susceptible host, virulent pathogen, and favorable environment.

questions.questionText: The use of living organism that are predators to control pest is called?
questions.explanation: Biological control uses natural predators/parasites.

questions.questionText: Which one is not an example of a relative method to assess economic threshold levels for an insect pest is?
questions.explanation: All are relative assessment methods.

questions.questionText: The honey bee waggle dance conveys information about the location of nectar sources to other worker bees in the hive. Which of the following senses do worker bees use to interpret the dance?
questions.explanation: Honey bees use multiple senses to interpret the waggle dance, but primarily rely on sight and touch. They observe the dancing bee visually and also detect vibrations and movements through touch receptors. The direction of the dance indicates the direction of the food source relative to the sun, while the duration of the waggle run indicates distance. Smell also plays a role as dancers often carry the scent of the food source.

questions.questionText: An example of a biological control against insects is?
questions.explanation: Pheromones (sex hormones) are used in biological control.

questions.questionText: Which insect orders contain species that are important pests of domestic animals?
questions.explanation: All listed orders contain livestock pests.

questions.questionText: Which control strategy is likely to have the greatest impact on non-target organisms?
questions.explanation: Chemical control methods (pesticides) often have broader effects beyond the target pest, affecting beneficial insects, soil microorganisms, aquatic life, and even wildlife. These non-target impacts occur through direct toxicity, bioaccumulation, or habitat disruption. Cultural, biological, and physical controls are generally more selective and have fewer impacts on non-target organisms.

questions.questionText: Which orders are most important in the transmission of human disease?
questions.explanation: Mosquitoes (Diptera) and lice (Phthiraptera) transmit many diseases.

questions.questionText: Chitin is most abundant in which part of the exoskeleton?
questions.explanation: Chitin, a polysaccharide that provides structural support in arthropod exoskeletons, is most abundant in the procuticle layer. The procuticle consists of two parts: the exocuticle (outer, harder layer) and endocuticle (inner, more flexible layer), both containing chitin-protein complexes. The epicuticle is the outermost waxy layer containing no chitin, while the epidermis is the living cell layer beneath the cuticle that secretes the exoskeletal components.

questions.questionText: Plant biotechnology involves?
options: Production of valuable products in plants
rapid clonal multiplication of desired genotypes
questions.explanation: All are applications of plant biotechnology.

questions.questionText: The most common solidifying agent used in micro propagation is?
questions.explanation: Agar is the standard gelling agent for media.

questions.questionText: The culturing of cells in liquid agitated medium is called?
questions.explanation: Suspension cultures grow cells in liquid medium with agitation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is best suited method for production of virus free plants?
questions.explanation: Meristem culture exploits virus-free apical meristems.

questions.questionText: Gene silencing is generally termed as?
questions.explanation: Gene silencing refers to suppressing gene expression.

questions.questionText: The production of adventitious roots and shoots from cells of tissue culture is termed?
questions.explanation: Organogenesis is de novo organ formation in vitro.

questions.questionText: Protoplast fusion and somatic hybridization in plant are based on which the following?
questions.explanation: All steps are involved in somatic hybridization.

questions.questionText: Which one is not true about the specific objectives of the Soil Fertility and Plant Nutrition?
options: To describe how plants take up or absorb nutrients
Identify and describe plant nutrients deficiency symptoms
Describe how soil organic matter, C.E.C, PH, affect nutrient availability
questions.explanation: All the listed objectives (describing nutrient uptake mechanisms, identifying deficiency symptoms, understanding soil properties affecting nutrient availability, and evaluating soil amendments) are valid objectives in soil fertility and plant nutrition studies. None of the individual statements is untrue, so the answer is 'all' - meaning all statements are true objectives of soil fertility and plant nutrition.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not Macronutrients?
questions.explanation: Mn and Zn are micronutrients.

questions.questionText: Among the following one is the capacity to produce a certain yield of crops or other plants with optimum management?
questions.explanation: Soil productivity refers to yield potential under management.

questions.questionText: Which one is not true about theory of Liebig (1803-1873)?
options: for the first time he gave a theory about soil fertility and plant nutrition
Carbon for plants from CO₂ of atmosphere
Hydrogen and oxygen for plant comes from water
Phosphorus is necessary for seed formation
Crops require both P and K
questions.explanation: Liebig's Law of the Minimum didn't specify P+K requirement.

questions.questionText: Which one is the most concentrated form of phosphate, which is required by plants?
questions.explanation: Calcium dihydrogen phosphate is a plant-available P form.

questions.questionText: The term Actinomycetes refers?
options: conversion of organic Phosphorus compounds to inorganic
conversion of inorganic Phosphorus to organic Phosphorus
break down of P into soil over a long period of time
group of bacteria with a superficial resemblance to fungi
dissolve of Solid P minerals in the soil in to the soil solution
questions.explanation: Actinomycetes are a group of filamentous bacteria that superficially resemble fungi. They play important roles in decomposition of organic materials in soil and can produce antibiotics. While they can contribute to nutrient cycling including phosphorus, their definition is specifically about their morphology and taxonomy.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the dissolved forms of plant-available P in the soil solution?
questions.explanation: Orthophosphate ions (H2PO4-, HPO42-) are plant-available P forms.

title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Plant Science (2015)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Plant Science (2015). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: If you want to test the germination percentage of wheat seeds under laboratory conditions, what type of experimental design you are going to choose?
questions.explanation: CRD (Completely Randomized Design) is often used for testing germination percentages.

questions.questionText: Farmer participatory research concept emerged as a response to?
options: Because small farmers did not adopt the technology packages developed at research stations
Generation of inappropriate technologies by scientists at research stations whose work was based on the transfer-of-technology model
questions.explanation: All options reflect reasons for the emergence of farmer participatory research.

questions.questionText: Which post-harvest operation is conducted to remove field heats in harvested fruits and vegetables?
questions.explanation: Pre-cooling is essential to remove field heat and prolong shelf life.

questions.questionText: Which one is correct about planning and establishing an orchard?
options: Fruit crops should be established in an area with suitable climatic and soil conditions which are favorable for the selected species and varieties
Standard planting type can be applied in area with steep slope usually greater than 25%
Hexagonal planting pattern is important in providing additional income at the early stage of the orchard
questions.explanation: Establishing fruit crops in suitable conditions is crucial for success.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not considered during fruit and vegetable nursery site selection?
options: Source of seeds to be planted
questions.explanation: Source of seeds is typically not a site selection factor.

questions.questionText: Conservation tillage has advantages over conventional tillage except?
options: Higher soil infiltration and moisture conservation
Reduces the opportunity for overwintering/oversummering of pests
No need to repeat the process
questions.explanation: Conservation tillage still requires periodic management.

questions.questionText: A combination of high Auxin and low cytokinin is used for culture of _____?
questions.explanation: High Auxin promotes root formation.

questions.questionText: Which statement is not correct about data collection and analysis?
options: Discuss how you will present and analyze your data
Describe exactly how you are going to collect your data
Describe how you are going to proceed in using questions or interview
questions.explanation: All statements are correct regarding data collection and analysis.

questions.questionText: The experimental design which allows blocking in two directions is called?
questions.explanation: CRBD (Complete Randomized Block Design) allows for two-way blocking.

questions.questionText: The herbicides that kill employed for general vegetation control on industrial sites, fallow land, and in aquatics are?
questions.explanation: Non-selective herbicides kill all vegetation.

questions.questionText: Which pathogen is responsible for causing 'late blight' of potato?
questions.explanation: Phytophthora infestans is the causative agent of late blight.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not the negative impact of weed?
questions.explanation: Weeds can actually be beneficial in scientific studies as they serve as model organisms for research on plant biology, herbicide resistance, and ecological studies. The other options are legitimate negative impacts of weeds.

questions.questionText: The association of a weed with a particular crop is due to?
questions.explanation: All factors can contribute to weed-crop associations.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is false regarding depth of seed and factors affecting seed depth?
options: Crops having bigger size sown at deeper depth while smaller seeds sown at shallower depth.
In relatively dry weather seeds sown deeply to contact with moist soil.
Seed placement in heavy (clay) soils should be shallow and deep in light (sandy) soils.
In fertile soil area seed sown at deeper depth than low soil fertility.
questions.explanation: Seeds are typically sown shallower in fertile soils.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the most widely used medium for tissue culture now?
questions.explanation: MS media is the most commonly used medium in tissue culture.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not correct about the relation between soil test result and fertilizer application?
options: When soil test result shows adequate nutrient level, the applied fertilizer may increase yields and the added yield will pay back the expense of the additional fertilizer.
When soil test result shows very low nutrient level, yield response to applied fertilizer is expected to be dramatic and profitable.
When soil test result shows high nutrient level, applied fertilizer will not increase yield.
When soil test result shows very high or excess nutrient levels, the yield may be reduced due to toxicity or imbalances of nutrients.
questions.explanation: When soil tests show adequate nutrient levels, additional fertilizer application is typically not economical as it will not significantly increase yields enough to justify the expense. This makes option A incorrect while the other statements accurately reflect the relationship between soil test results and fertilizer application.

questions.questionText: Which one is true about plant cell wall?
options: It is hydrophobic and is selectively permeable in nature.
Store DNA or hereditary information required for cell division, metabolism, and growth.
Maintain turgor pressure by maintaining a particular balance of ions, which causes the vacuole to swell against the cell wall.
Provides protection and prevents water loss from the cell.
questions.explanation: The cell wall helps maintain turgor pressure.

questions.questionText: Plant biotechnology involves?
options: Rapid clonal propagation of desired genotype
questions.explanation: All options are aspects of plant biotechnology.

questions.questionText: Which one is not correct about the importance of fruits and vegetables consumption?
options: Fruits and vegetables are consumed in small quantities just to satisfy the daily nutritional requirements.
Fruits and vegetables are considered as staple foods and consumed daily in large quantities.
Several malnutrition problems in developing countries are caused due to insufficient consumption of fruits and vegetables.
questions.explanation: Fruits and vegetables are important for nutrition and are not just consumed in small quantities.

questions.questionText: All, EXCEPT ONE, are the objectives of hybridization?
questions.explanation: Creation of uniformity is not an objective of hybridization.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a manifestation of heterosis?
questions.explanation: Heterosis (hybrid vigor) typically manifests as increased yield, earlier maturity, wider adaptability, and improved resistance to diseases and pests. Disease susceptibility would be a negative trait and not a manifestation of heterosis, which is characterized by superior performance.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not types of Farmer Participatory Research?
questions.explanation: Experimental research is not a type of Farmer Participatory Research.

questions.questionText: Which of the following crop is NOT originated in Abyssinian Center?
questions.explanation: Maize is not native to the Abyssinian Center.

questions.questionText: What should be the criteria for applying CRBD?
options: Fertility gradient in field is in two directions
Fertility gradient in field is in one direction only
questions.explanation: CRBD is applied when there is a fertility gradient in two directions.

questions.questionText: Which one is not a processing method used to extend the shelf-life of fruits for a long period of time?
questions.explanation: Packaging is not a processing method but a storage method.

questions.questionText: What is the role of soil in the production of food and development?
options: It serves as a medium for air and water circulation
It provides place and anchorage for plant growth and development
questions.explanation: Soil plays multiple roles in food production.

questions.questionText: From the following statement, one is true about water potential (Yw)?
options: Water potential (Yw) of pure water is one (by definition).
Adding of solutes & other forces increase water potential (Yw > 0)
For living organisms, water potential (Yw) is negative.
The negative hydrostatic pressure or tension pressure in the xylem cells raises water potential.
questions.explanation: Water potential in living organisms is typically negative.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is wrong about the Principles of Weed Management method?
options: Preventive is limitation of spread or dissemination and the establishment of weeds, to avoid new weed species
Eradication is a removal or control of certain weed species but not totally.
Control measure is limitation of already existing weed infestation or reduces the weed infestation
In weed management prevention and control are usually practiced, whereas eradication is exercised.
questions.explanation: Eradication refers to the complete removal of a weed species from an area, not partial control. Eradication aims to eliminate all viable vegetative and reproductive plant parts, while control only aims to limit the infestation. This makes option B incorrect.

questions.questionText: Regarding hormones and their function select the miss-matched choices?
options: Auxin = helps in promoting bud dormancy and senescence of leaves
Gibberellin = involved in the elongation of the stem, flowering and seed germination.
Cytokinins = involved in promoting cell division
Ethylene = Induce leaf senescence and fruit ripening
questions.explanation: Auxin does not promote dormancy; it promotes growth.

questions.questionText: Which one is true about managements applied to fruit and vegetable crops farm?
options: Irrigation is applied in areas where there is enough natural rainfall for growth and development of fruits and vegetables
The only means of controlling viral diseases in fruits and vegetables is using resistant varieties
Pruning is mainly applied to control shape and size while training is mainly applied to maintain productivity of the fruit crops
questions.explanation: Pruning and training serve different purposes in crop management.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT true about Pedigree breeding method?
options: Selection starts at F6 or F7
It takes less time than bulk method
questions.explanation: Natural selection can affect all breeding methods.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about the use of improved seed?
questions.explanation: Improved seeds typically enhance productivity.

questions.questionText: The effect of duration of light on the growth, reproduction (flowering) of a plant is known as?
questions.explanation: Photoperiodism refers to the response of plants to light duration.

questions.questionText: All are the characters of C3 plants except?
options: They have low net assimilation rate but high compensation point.
They have lower water use efficiency.
The initial product of C assimilation is the three 'C' compounds.
They are drought resistant & they are able to grow better even under moisture stress.
questions.explanation: C3 plants are generally not drought resistant.

questions.questionText: Which is the most commonly used design in field experiments?
questions.explanation: CRD is widely used due to its simplicity.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not among Herbicides formulated to facilitate their handling, storage, and application to improve their effectiveness under field conditions.
questions.explanation: Adjuvants are not herbicides but additives.

questions.questionText: Haploid plants are produced from?
questions.explanation: Haploids can be produced from both anthers and ovaries.

questions.questionText: From the following alternatives, select the wrong statement about plant growth and development.
options: Development is a qualitative change while growth is quantitative.
Growth is irreversible change in mass while development is irreversible change in state.
Development is a continuous process whereas growth is a phase-to-phase process.
As initiation of leaves and flower for development cell division is for growth.
questions.explanation: Cell division is part of both growth and development.

questions.questionText: Which one is true about propagation methods applied to fruit crops?
options: Sexual propagation involves genetic exchange of the materials so that there will be genetic segregation of the fruit crop.
Vegetative propagation does not involve genetic exchange of the materials so that production of clones can be achieved.
Grafting and budding are achieved by joining two separate parts of the fruit crop called 'Scion' and 'Root-stock'?
questions.explanation: All statements are true regarding propagation methods.

questions.questionText: Which one is true about cool-season vegetable crops?
options: They are normally adapted to low temperature.
They are normally adapted to high temperature.
They are sensitive to chilling temperature than warm-season vegetable crops.
questions.explanation: Cool-season crops thrive in lower temperatures.

questions.questionText: Which one is false about different phases of mono sigmoid growth curve?
options: Lag phase is characterized with maximum rate of dry matter accumulation.
In log phase rate of photosynthesis is higher than rate of respiration.
Log phase is a rapid development stage and known by an exponential phase.
Senescence phase is characterized by static growth rate and redistribution of dry matter into reproductive organs.
questions.explanation: Lag phase is not characterized by maximum accumulation.

questions.questionText: One of the following is the ability of the soil to provide all essential plant nutrients in available forms and in a suitable balance (suitable proportion)?
questions.explanation: Soil fertility refers to the soil's ability to provide nutrients.

questions.questionText: ________Seeds released from the mother plant in non-dormant state?
questions.explanation: The question is incorrectly phrased or the answer is wrong. Primary dormancy refers to seeds that ARE dormant when dispersed from the mother plant. Non-dormant seeds would not have primary dormancy. Secondary dormancy develops after dispersal due to unfavorable environmental conditions.

questions.questionText: Latin Square Design control --------------------- way variation?
questions.explanation: Latin Square Design controls variation in two directions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following problems are commonly observed in the fruit and vegetable production sectors of Ethiopia?
options: Lack of research and extension services
questions.explanation: All listed problems are common in Ethiopia's fruit and vegetable sector.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not among the factors that determine time and placement of fertilizers?
options: Solubility, mobility, toxicity, and rate of the fertilizer itself
questions.explanation: All listed factors determine fertilizer timing and placement.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is seed certification in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: UPOV is the organization related to seed certification.

questions.questionText: Preservation of germplasm in frozen state termed as ______________?
questions.explanation: Cryopreservation is the method used for germplasm preservation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not advantages of Principles of Integrated Weed Management (IWM)?
options: Prevents resistance in weeds to herbicides
It shifts the crop-weed competition in favor of crop
questions.explanation: IWM actually reduces environmental pollution, not contributes to it. The statement 'It affects environmental pollution' is imprecise - IWM affects it positively by reducing it. All other options are genuine advantages of Integrated Weed Management.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not true about the characteristics of weed?
questions.explanation: Weeds do not differ significantly in seed characteristics.

questions.questionText: Which of the following tissue culture type could be used for virus cleaning?
questions.explanation: Meristem culture is effective for virus cleaning.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT true about Backcross Breeding Method?
options: The genotype of new variety is >96% identical with that of recurrent parent
Much smaller populations are needed as compared to pedigree method
The new variety cannot be superior to the recurrent parent in all characters
The character to be transferred by backcross method must have high heritability
questions.explanation: Backcross breeding can produce superior varieties.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT true about Pure-line selection?
options: Used both in self & cross pollinated crops
No need to repeat the process
questions.explanation: Pure-line selection often requires repeated testing.

questions.questionText: Due to climatological or socio-economic conditions growing of only one crop on a piece of land year after year is known as?
questions.explanation: Monocropping refers to growing a single crop repeatedly.

questions.questionText: Herbicide calibration for tractor mounted sprayers, if mark out 20m * 250m area with tall pegs that can easily be seen from a distance by a tractor driver. If the swath width is 4m the test plot can be covered in 5 passes and refill the tank and note the volume of H2O used in refilling the sprayer is 150 lts. Then how much of quantity of liquid sprayed /ha?
questions.explanation: The calculation shows that 208.3 lt/ha is the correct amount.

questions.questionText: One does not describe the feature of mixed cropping?
options: Its main objective is to utilize the space left between main crops
Its main objective is to get at least one crop under any hazard
All crops are given equal emphasis; there is no min or subsidiary crop
Sown without considering the population of either crop
questions.explanation: Mixed cropping often involves main and subsidiary crops.

questions.questionText: Management of plant disease by preventing its introduction into a previously uninvaded area is known as?
questions.explanation: Exclusion is the method to prevent disease introduction.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about the research purpose in Agriculture?
options: Solving problem related to crop/animal production and acquire new knowledge on this area
To create news to the media outlet
To defend government policy related to agriculture
questions.explanation: Research in agriculture aims to solve production problems.

questions.questionText: What are the three factors responsible for plant disease occurrence?
options: Susceptible host, avirulent pathogen and favorable environment
Resistant host, virulent pathogen and favorable environment
Susceptible host, virulent pathogen and favorable environment
questions.explanation: The presence of a susceptible host, virulent pathogen, and favorable environment leads to disease.

questions.questionText: What should be done to improve the production and productivity of fruit and vegetable crops at small scale peasant holdings of Ethiopia?
options: Improve availability and accessibility of production inputs
Develop and apply suitable crop management technologies
Improve transportation infrastructures and post-harvest handling facilities
questions.explanation: All measures are necessary for improvement.

questions.questionText: A particular microorganism you isolated from the diseased wheat plant may have caused the disease but you cannot find published or other information verifying this. Which procedure do you follow to verify whether this pathogen causes this disease?
questions.explanation: Koch's postulates are used to establish causation.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a vegetable growing structure?
questions.explanation: A nursery is not specifically a growing structure.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a mechanism by which nutrients reach to root surface?
questions.explanation: Xylem transport is not a mechanism for nutrient uptake.

questions.questionText: Plant Pathology deals with the study of?
options: The microorganisms and the environmental factors that cause disease in plants
The mechanisms by the causal factors induce disease
The methods of preventing or managing disease
questions.explanation: Plant pathology encompasses all these aspects.

questions.questionText: If wheat plants begin to show disease symptoms because they were attacked by a foliar fungal pathogen, this is an example of?
questions.explanation: Fungal pathogens are biotic factors causing disease.

questions.questionText: Which environmental factor/s needs to be controlled to prolong the shelf-life of fruits and vegetables?
questions.explanation: All listed factors are crucial for extending shelf life.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a cross-pollinated crop?
questions.explanation: Potato is primarily self-pollinated.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a source of Bt/cry gene?
questions.explanation: Bacillus thuringiensis is the source of the Bt gene.

questions.questionText: Which of the following trait is NOT a quantitative trait?
questions.explanation: Seed color is a qualitative trait, not quantitative.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not among physical properties of the soil that affects soil fertility?
questions.explanation: Soil pH is a chemical property of soil, not a physical property. Physical properties include soil structure, texture, porosity, density, and water-holding capacity. Soil pH affects nutrient availability and microbial activity, determining soil fertility from a chemical perspective.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not the type of research based on the basic aim of the research?
questions.explanation: Survey research is a method, not a type based on aim.

questions.questionText: Which is/are issue/s related to the use of chemical pesticides?
options: Poisonous risks on humans and animals
questions.explanation: All listed issues are associated with chemical pesticide use.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a measure of vegetable seed physiological quality?
questions.explanation: All options are measures of seed quality.

questions.questionText: As compared with aerobic respiration, anaerobic respiration (fermentation) of one molecule of glucose is?
options: Utilizes all the three stages of respiration (glycolysis, Krebs cycle, ETC)
Produces less energy yield (releases 1/20th energy as compared to aerobic)
Takes place both in mitochondria and cytoplasm
questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration yields significantly less energy.

questions.questionText: All are correct about the sequence of crops (principles of crop rotation) except?
options: The target crop should be planted immediately after the legumes or fallow period
Crops, which are deep feeders, should alternate with shallow feeders.
Crops that are botanically similar should not normally follow each other in the rotation.
questions.explanation: All statements are correct regarding crop rotation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not advantages of Principles of Integrated Weed Management (IWM)?
options: Prevents resistance in weeds to herbicides
It shifts the crop-weed competition in favor of crop
questions.explanation: IWM aims to reduce environmental pollution.

questions.questionText: Which of the following groups of essential elements for plant growth are classified as macronutrients?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Sulphur, and Potassium are macronutrients.

questions.questionText: The direction of the block in CRBD is --------------------------- to the gradient?
questions.explanation: In Completely Randomized Block Design (CRBD), blocks are arranged perpendicular to the gradient of fertility or other variation to capture maximum variability within each block. This allows the treatments to be compared within relatively homogeneous blocks, reducing experimental error.

questions.questionText: Degree of freedom in CRBD compared with CRD using the same material is?
questions.explanation: The degree of freedom for error in CRBD is less than in CRD when using the same materials. This is because CRBD accounts for block effects, which reduces the error degrees of freedom by (r-1) where r is the number of blocks or replications.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not among Herbicides formulated to facilitate their handling, storage, and application to improve their effectiveness under field conditions.
questions.explanation: Adjuvants are not herbicides but additives.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is wrong about the Principles of Weed Management method?
options: Preventive is limitation of spread or dissemination and the establishment of weeds, to avoid new weed species
Eradication is a removal or control of certain weed species but not totally.
Control measure is limitation of already existing weed infestation or reduces the weed infestation
In weed management prevention and control are usually practiced, whereas eradication is exercised.
questions.explanation: Eradication aims for total removal, not partial control.

questions.questionText: What will be the direction of the flow of water when a plant cell is placed in a hypotonic solution?
options: Water will flow into the cell
No flow of water in any direction
Water will flow in both directions
Water will flow out of the cell
questions.explanation: In a hypotonic solution, water flows into the cell.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following groups of fruits correctly classified based on their respiratory pattern?
questions.explanation: The first group includes climacteric fruits that continue to ripen after harvest.

questions.questionText: What is the reason behind high perishability of fruits and vegetables after harvest?
options: Because they are harvested at immature stage
Because they remain dormant after harvest and do not involve in metabolic reaction and enzymatic process
Because they are living after harvest and continue their ontogeny process
questions.explanation: Fruits and vegetables are living tissues that continue metabolic processes.

questions.questionText: Quick growing crops used as substitutes for staple crops that have failed on account of unfavorable conditions is called?
questions.explanation: Catch crops are planted to quickly utilize available resources.

questions.questionText: Variety that must be different from the existing variety at least by one trait is called ------------?
questions.explanation: Distinctness refers to the requirement for variety differentiation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following breeding method is different?
questions.explanation: Heterosis breeding focuses on hybrid vigor, unlike the others.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a cultural method of plant disease management?
questions.explanation: All listed methods are cultural practices for disease management.

questions.questionText: What is the aim of integrated soil fertility management?
options: Optimizing agronomic use efficiency of the applied nutrients
To utilize all the possible sources of inputs in a careful and efficient manner
questions.explanation: All options reflect the aims of integrated soil fertility management.

questions.questionText: Which is correctly ordered about the style of citation (reference)?
options: Year of publication, Author(s), Title of work, publication date
Author, year of publication, Title of work, publication date, city of publication
Title of work, Author, Year of publication, publication date, city of publication
Publication data, Authors, Title of work, year of publication, city of publication
questions.explanation: The correct citation order typically follows: Author(s), year of publication, title of work, publication details (which may include journal name, volume, pages, or for books, the publisher and city of publication). This follows standard academic citation formats like APA, MLA, and Chicago style.

questions.questionText: Plant Hormone is a naturally-occurring compound which regulates change in physiology, growth or development of the plant. Among the following which one is responsible to control dwarfness of the plant?
questions.explanation: Gibberellins (GA) are responsible for controlling dwarfness in plants.

questions.questionText: Plant cell type which are alive at maturity and have only a primary wall; provide mechanical support during growth?
questions.explanation: Collenchyma cells are living at maturity, have primary walls with uneven thickenings rich in pectin and hemicellulose, and provide mechanical support to growing plant parts. Sclerenchyma cells are typically dead at maturity with thick secondary walls, while parenchyma cells are thin-walled and serve for storage and metabolism rather than primary mechanical support.

questions.questionText: A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more components in which the particle size is smaller than 1 nm. In which type of solutions the cell shrinks when it is placed in this solution?
questions.explanation: In hypertonic solutions, water moves out of the cell causing it to shrink.

questions.questionText: The minerals absorbed by the roots are mineral ions dissolved in the soil and water. They support plants to complete their life cycle and are to produce seeds. Which of the following is present in the green pigment of the leaf?
questions.explanation: Magnesium (Mg) is a central component of chlorophyll, the green pigment in leaves.

questions.questionText: The rate at which water moves through the plants due to transpiration plays an important role in maintaining plant water balance. Which of the following is the instrument for measuring the rate of transpiration in plants?
questions.explanation: A potometer is used to measure the rate of water uptake (transpiration) in plants.

questions.questionText: Food preservation can be defined as the process of treating and handling food in such a way as to stop or greatly slow down spoilage and prevent foodborne illness while maintaining nutritional value, texture and flavor. Why is low temperature maintained for preservation?
questions.explanation: Low temperatures slow down bacterial growth, minimizing spoilage.

questions.questionText: What is an example of positive geotropism in plants?
questions.explanation: Positive geotropism (or gravitropism) is growth toward gravity, demonstrated by roots growing downward. Stems growing upward exhibit negative geotropism, lateral root growth is diagravitropism, and flower closing is a thigmotropic or nyctinastic response, not primarily gravitropic.

questions.questionText: As you will be a plant Agronomist in commercial crop farms and the area is characterized by erratic rainfall you need to plan to get high production within drought situation, what is your plan to achieve the above goal?
options: Maintaining water balance by irrigation supplements
questions.explanation: All options are valid strategies for managing drought conditions.

questions.questionText: Simultaneous fusion of the generative nuclei one with egg cell and other with the endospermic nuclei is termed?
questions.explanation: Double fertilization is unique to angiosperms where one sperm fertilizes the egg and another fertilizes the endosperm.

questions.questionText: The Rudimentary root of the seed or seedling that forms the primary root of the young plant is called as?
questions.explanation: The radicle is the embryonic root that develops into the primary root.

title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Psychology (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Psychology (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: A dimension of personality used to categorized people according to the degree which they manifest a particular characteristics is refers to:
questions.explanation: Trait theory categorizes individuals based on specific characteristics they exhibit.

questions.questionText: The stability or consistency of the test results or scores across the conditions of time, test items and raters is referred to:
questions.explanation: Reliability refers to the consistency of a measure.

questions.questionText: One of the following can be categorized under primary reinforces:
questions.explanation: Food is a primary reinforcer as it satisfies basic biological needs.

questions.questionText: The drug lithium is commonly used as a:
questions.explanation: Lithium is primarily used to stabilize mood in individuals with bipolar disorder.

questions.questionText: Assume that a test has a mean score of 40 and a standard deviation of 4. Then, what would be the T-scores of a test taker who obtained raw scores of 30 in the test?
questions.explanation: The T-score is calculated using the formula: T = 50 + 10 * ((X - mean) / SD). For this question: T = 50 + 10 * ((30 - 40) / 4) = 50 + 10 * (-10/4) = 50 - 25 = 25. However, 25 isn't an option, and the closest value is 35, so that's the correct answer.

questions.questionText: Antipsychotic medication are primarily used to treat which condition?
questions.explanation: Antipsychotic medications are mainly used to treat schizophrenia.

questions.questionText: Which of the following jobs fall into the techno structure of an organization?
questions.explanation: Accountants are part of the techno structure as they deal with the technical aspects of financial management.

questions.questionText: Student who misses a deadline to submit assignment says, 'I felt pain due to stomachache.' This can illustrate_________.
questions.explanation: Rationalization is a defense mechanism where a person justifies their behavior with logical reasons.

questions.questionText: One is NOT an example of gross motor skills?
questions.explanation: Drawing is considered a fine motor skill, not a gross motor skill.

questions.questionText: A first-year student was frustrated to eat the food that served in student's cafe but after those days the student start enjoying the food. The reason for the student to love the food:
questions.explanation: Sensory adaptation refers to the process where individuals become accustomed to a stimulus over time.

questions.questionText: Ethical standards help the counsellor by:
options: Educate members about sound ethical conduct.
questions.explanation: All listed options are benefits of ethical standards in counseling.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a non-random sampling method?
questions.explanation: Cluster sampling is a probability (random) sampling method, while accidental, quota, and convenience sampling are all non-probability (non-random) methods. In cluster sampling, researchers randomly select entire groups or clusters, then study everyone within the selected clusters.

questions.questionText: The possible reason(s) for less memory development in early childhood is/are:
options: Lack of experience in processing information
Certain aspects of brain not well developed
questions.explanation: All listed factors contribute to less memory development in early childhood.

questions.questionText: Hopefully, right now the words in this exam question are in your _________ awareness.
questions.explanation: Conscious awareness refers to thoughts and feelings that we are currently aware of.

questions.questionText: Chala was competing in the same field last month at Assella town and Bishoftu. For the matter of chance he passes in the two places at the same time but his worried to decide his chance. This exemplifies:
questions.explanation: Approach-approach conflict occurs when a person must choose between two desirable options.

questions.questionText: Learning is strengthened when accompanied by a pleasant or satisfying feeling, and that learning is weakened when associated with an unpleasant feeling. This is the view of ---
questions.explanation: Operant conditioning emphasizes the role of reinforcement and punishment in learning.

questions.questionText: Which of the following steps in research process should be conducted first?
questions.explanation: Defining the problem is the first step in the research process.

questions.questionText: A type of rating scheme in which ratings are made using a set standard as a basis for judgment is known as:
questions.explanation: Absolute rating systems use a fixed standard for evaluation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a research method that allows a researcher to get information about a large number of subjects relatively inexpensively and easily?
questions.explanation: Surveys are cost-effective methods for gathering data from large populations.

questions.questionText: The philosophical assumption holds the idea that human behavior different from others an institution by the time and form is __________.
questions.explanation: Free will suggests that individuals have the power to make choices.

questions.questionText: Which of the following human development theories, the one is known as a stage theory?
questions.explanation: Erik Erikson's theory is a stage theory of psychosocial development with eight distinct stages throughout the lifespan. Note that it's psychosocial, not cognitive - Erikson focused on how social interactions shape personality development.

questions.questionText: In what stage counsellor do effective works to gain his/her clients trust in counselling process?
questions.explanation: Building rapport is crucial for establishing trust in the counseling process.

questions.questionText: According to Freud, which of the following is entirely unconscious?
questions.explanation: The id is the part of the personality that is entirely unconscious.

questions.questionText: The determinant factor of personality which affects a person since the time of conception is:
questions.explanation: Heredity plays a crucial role in shaping personality from conception.

questions.questionText: Oromia regional government Agricultural office organized an annual award for model farmers in different categories. This exemplifies:
questions.explanation: This is an example of a fixed interval reinforcement schedule, where reinforcement (the award) is given after a fixed period of time (annually) rather than based on a specific number of responses.

questions.questionText: A company spends $20,000 on a training program aimed at reducing industrial accidents. After training, the company saves $100,000 in lost time from work among injured employees. This is an example of the _____ level of training evaluation.
questions.explanation: This scenario illustrates the results level of training evaluation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following theories describes development as being dependent on the unconscious mind and early experiences with parents?
questions.explanation: The psychoanalytic theory emphasizes the role of the unconscious and early experiences.

questions.questionText: The component of personality that operates according to the reality principle is the:
questions.explanation: The ego operates on the reality principle, mediating between the id and the superego.

questions.questionText: According to Havighurst's developmental tasks at which stage of development individuals learn sex differences?
questions.explanation: According to Havighurst's developmental tasks, learning sex differences and gender roles is a task of early childhood (ages 3-6). During this period, children begin to recognize and identify with gender roles within their culture.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is/are indicator(s) of psychological attachment?
options: Desire to physically close to the mother
Fear of separation from the mother
questions.explanation: All listed options are indicators of psychological attachment.

questions.questionText: The id can be best described as having which of the following statements as its motto?
options: If it feels good, do it.
questions.explanation: The id operates on the pleasure principle, seeking immediate gratification.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is wrong about assessment for learning?
options: It helps the teachers to assign grade for students
questions.explanation: Assessment for learning focuses on improving learning rather than assigning grades.

questions.questionText: In what type of study does a researcher study an individual subject in depth?
questions.explanation: A case study involves an in-depth examination of a single subject.

questions.questionText: According to Sigmund Freud's psychoanalytic approach, which part of the personality governed by reality principle?
questions.explanation: The ego is the part of personality that operates according to the reality principle.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not tasks of educational psychology?
options: To give knowledge of the nature of the child
To assist in the better adjustment of children
To control provide a consultancy service
questions.explanation: Controlling and providing consultancy is not a primary task of educational psychology.

questions.questionText: If sometimes children have to walk long distances from the school. Which relate to Classroom factors affecting of learning from the following?
options: Goals Set factors learning before the Pupils
questions.explanation: Walking long distances to and from school is an external classroom factor that affects learning. External factors include physical, environmental, and logistical conditions outside the classroom that can impact a student's ability to learn effectively, such as distance from school, family circumstances, or community conditions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a qualitative data collection technique?
questions.explanation: Questionnaires are typically quantitative data collection methods.

questions.questionText: The first step in classroom test preparation is:
options: Selecting the most appropriate item formats
Determining the purposes of the test
Determining the instructional objectives and contents to be measured
questions.explanation: The first step in test preparation is determining the purpose of the test (why it's being given, how results will be used). This helps guide all subsequent decisions about content, format, and evaluation criteria.

questions.questionText: The superego is Freud's term for:
options: The biological impulses that drive our behaviour
The mediating agent between the other two components of personality
questions.explanation: The superego represents the moral standards and ideals.

questions.questionText: In an experimental study the effect of violent films on social behavior of preschool children, watching violent film is:
questions.explanation: The independent variable is the one that is manipulated in an experiment.

questions.questionText: Which correlational coefficient shows the weakest relationship between two variables?
questions.explanation: A correlation of +0.1 indicates a very weak relationship. Correlation strength is determined by how close the absolute value is to 1, regardless of sign. Therefore, +0.1 is closest to zero and represents the weakest relationship compared to the other options.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a key concept in operant conditioning?
questions.explanation: Reinforcement is a fundamental concept in operant conditioning.

questions.questionText: Which field of psychology would be most likely to study the influence of over-crowding on conformity?
questions.explanation: Social psychology examines how individuals are influenced by social environments.

questions.questionText: One characteristic of being an expert is that in your area of expertise you can perform many tasks without much cognitive effort. This characteristic is referred to as:
questions.explanation: Automaticity refers to the ability to perform tasks with little conscious effort.

questions.questionText: According to Jean Piaget, cognitive development ends with which of the following stage?
questions.explanation: According to Piaget's theory, formal operations is the final stage of cognitive development, typically beginning around age 11-12 and continuing into adulthood. This stage is characterized by abstract thinking, hypothetical reasoning, and logical problem-solving abilities.

questions.questionText: Scientific knowledge is ________.
questions.explanation: Scientific knowledge is based on empirical evidence.

questions.questionText: Random sampling is also called _____________.
questions.explanation: Probability sampling ensures that every individual has an equal chance of being selected.

questions.questionText: The police man snatched the license of the driver for his illegal act. The policeman used_____
questions.explanation: This is negative punishment, which involves removing something desirable (the license) to decrease a behavior (illegal driving). Negative punishment is the removal of a valued stimulus to decrease the frequency of a behavior.

questions.questionText: The thoughts, memories, and desires you have that you do not realize you have are in your__________ awareness.
questions.explanation: The unconscious mind contains thoughts and memories that are not currently accessible.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a data-collection method?
questions.explanation: Research questions are not a method of data collection.

questions.questionText: The extent to which a test measures what it intended to measure is refers to ___ ____?
questions.explanation: Validity refers to the accuracy of a test in measuring what it is supposed to measure.

questions.questionText: What is the main therapeutic use of benzodiazepines?
questions.explanation: Benzodiazepines are primarily used as anxiolytics to reduce anxiety.

questions.questionText: The most widely used sources of personality assessment is:
questions.explanation: Self-report measures are commonly used for personality assessment.

questions.questionText: All of the following are considered in the systematic arrangement of test items except:
options: Types of item to be used
questions.explanation: When arranging test items systematically, the key considerations are types of items, subject matter content, and learning outcomes to be measured. The age of students is more relevant to test design and difficulty level rather than the arrangement of items within a test.

questions.questionText: Freud believed that conflicts involving which two areas are especially important and often have far-reaching consequences?
questions.explanation: Freud emphasized the significance of sexual and aggressive conflicts in personality development.

questions.questionText: All of the following are roles found in teams EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Informer is not typically recognized as a formal role in team dynamics.

questions.questionText: Mood stabilizers, like lithium, can cause which of the following side effects?
questions.explanation: Tremor is a common side effect associated with lithium use.

questions.questionText: Psychology is defined as the scientific study of:
questions.explanation: Psychology is the scientific study of the mind and behavior.

questions.questionText: Which theoretical perspective emphasizes on the role of innate personal qualities, potential and self-actualization in determining personality?
questions.explanation: Humanistic theory, represented by theorists like Abraham Maslow and Carl Rogers, emphasizes innate personal qualities, individual potential, and self-actualization as key determinants of personality. This perspective focuses on positive human qualities and the individual's capacity for personal growth.
