questions.questionText: A 65 year-old patient sustained a fall down accident three hours prior to presenting to the Emergency Room. He fell down with the arms extended. On examination, vital signs were normal with a right wrist deformity. X-ray showed displaced Colles' fracture. Which one is the best management option?
options: Skin traction for few days then casting
questions.explanation: Closed reduction and casting is the standard treatment for a Colles' fracture.

questions.questionText: A manager of a health center wants to provide BCG vaccine for infants on Fridays. Which of the following is the best management function that the manager used?
questions.explanation: Planning is essential for scheduling vaccination sessions.

questions.questionText: A 29 year-old man comes to emergency clinic with crampy abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea of one day. Stool microscopy shows trophozoites. Which one of the following is most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Entamoeba histolytica causes amoebic dysentery characterized by bloody diarrhea.

questions.questionText: A 22 year-old nulliparous woman at 42+3 weeks gestation has a Bishop's score of 8. Which of the following would be the most appropriate induction method for this patient?
questions.explanation: With a favorable Bishop's score of 8 (indicating a ripe cervix), oxytocin is the most appropriate induction method. A Bishop's score of 10 would be unusually high for a nulliparous woman, so 8 is more realistic and still indicates a favorable cervix for induction.

questions.questionText: During a school survey on refraction, a 6 year-old girl was found to have a refractive error of (+3) on the left eye while the right eye was (+6). If the refractive error is not corrected by spectacles, which of the following is LEAST expected to happen?
questions.explanation: Floaters are not typically a consequence of uncorrected refractive errors.

questions.questionText: A 60 year-old alcoholic patient presented with fever, headache and neck pain of two days duration. On examination, body T=39°C and has neck stiffness. Bacterial meningitis was suspected but lumbar puncture was deferred because he has papilledema. Which one of the following is the best empiric therapy for this patient in addition to ampicillin?
questions.explanation: Ceftriaxone and vancomycin provide broad coverage for suspected bacterial meningitis.

questions.questionText: A 27 year-old woman complains of fever and fatigue. Non-tender, enlarged cervical and axillary lymph nodes are noted. Chest X-ray shows hilar lymphadenopathy and diffuse interstitial infiltrates. Lymph node biopsy shows non-caseating granuloma. Which drug is the most appropriate therapy?
questions.explanation: Glucocorticoids are effective in treating sarcoidosis.

questions.questionText: A 66 year-old diabetic man suddenly collapsed in a hospital cafeteria and quick evaluation revealed an unresponsive man with no respiratory effort and pulseless carotids. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The absence of respiratory effort and pulselessness indicates cardiac arrest.

questions.questionText: A communal well water source development project was planned to be developed in a rural village. What needs to be identified for the outcome of the project to be effective?
options: Acceptance of the water source by the community
Cost of materials for development purpose
Electrolyte composition of the water source
Level of trace minerals in the water source
questions.explanation: Community acceptance is crucial for the success of water source projects.

questions.questionText: A 60 year old man who had been smoking a pack of cigarettes daily for the last twenty years presented with one year history of increasing dyspnea on exertion and accumulation dry cough. Chest examination reveals hyper-resonance all over the lungs and decreased breath sounds. Which of the following is most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Emphysema is characterized by hyper-resonance and decreased breath sounds.

title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Public Health Officer (2015)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Public Health Officer (2015). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: A 21 yrs old male pt. came with compliant of productive cough of one month duration. He also has low grade fever, night sweat, weight loss & loss of appetite. On examination he is chronically sick looking with vital signs in the normal range. He has no remarkable syndromes. Laboratory investigation of Sputum microscopy showed mycobacterium bacilli. What is the best next step of the management of the pt?
questions.explanation: The best next step is to start anti-tuberculosis treatment immediately. The patient has all the classical symptoms of TB (productive cough >2 weeks, fever, night sweats, weight loss) and the diagnosis is confirmed by sputum microscopy showing mycobacterium bacilli. According to WHO and national TB guidelines, treatment should start immediately upon confirmed diagnosis.

questions.questionText: A 40yr old known RVI pt. who has been on ART for the last three yrs came with a compliant of whitish coating over his tongue with difficulty & pain during swallowing of two wks duration. What is the WHO clinical stage of the pt?
questions.explanation: The clinical presentation suggests oral candidiasis (thrush) which is consistent with WHO Clinical Stage III. Oral candidiasis is characterized by whitish coating and painful swallowing, and is an opportunistic infection that indicates moderate immunosuppression. Stage III includes oral candidiasis as one of its defining conditions for adults with HIV.

questions.questionText: A 20 yr old male came with complaints of on and off type high grade fever of five days duration. He also has history of headache and arthralgia. What is the drug of choice for the management of this pt?
questions.explanation: Doxycycline is the drug of choice for treating suspected rickettsial infections, which commonly present with high-grade fever, headache, and arthralgia. It's also effective against many other febrile illnesses including Q fever, Lyme disease, and certain forms of typhus. Without other specific symptoms to suggest an alternative diagnosis, doxycycline provides broad coverage for the most likely pathogens.

questions.questionText: A 30 yr old male pt. came to a clinic after he sustained a nail prick injury at his leg while working at a construction site a day back. What is the most appropriate next step in the management of this pt?
questions.explanation: For a penetrating wound like a nail prick that is contaminated and at high risk for tetanus, tetanus immunoglobulin (TIG) is the appropriate immediate management, especially if the patient's vaccination status is unknown or inadequate. TIG provides passive immunity against tetanus. This should be followed by wound cleaning and consideration of tetanus toxoid vaccination based on the patient's immunization history.

questions.questionText: A 34 yr old male pt came with a compliant of burning epigastric pain of two wks duration. What is the most likely anticipated complication in this pt?
questions.explanation: Gastrointestinal bleeding is a common complication in such cases.

questions.questionText: A 26 yrs old male presented with complaints of bloody diarrhea & fever of 12 hrs duration. What is the most likely diagnosis of this pt?
questions.explanation: The symptoms are consistent with Shigellosis.

questions.questionText: A 54 yr old male came with a complaint of abdominal distention of one month duration. What is the most likely diagnosis of this pt?
options: Chronic liver disease 2 o to Autoimmune hepatitis
Chronic liver disease 2 o to Chronic Viral hepatitis
Chronic liver disease 2 o to drug induced hepatitis
Chronic liver disease 2 o to alcoholic hepatitis
questions.explanation: Chronic liver disease due to viral hepatitis is common.

questions.questionText: A 24 yr old male came with a compliant of cough of seven days duration. What is the next best step to the management of this pt?
questions.explanation: Ceftriaxone is appropriate for severe pneumonia.

questions.questionText: A 28 yr old male presented with complaints of shortness of breath & dry cough of two wks duration. Physical examination reveals dullness to percussion over the lower lung fields bilaterally. What is the most likely explanation for this finding?
questions.explanation: Pleural effusion is indicated by dullness on percussion over the lower lung fields. This physical finding, combined with shortness of breath and dry cough, is most consistent with pleural effusion.

questions.questionText: A 29 yr old female who is known asthmatic pt. on intermittent Salbutamol puff came for routine follow up. What is the most appropriate step to the management of this pt?
questions.explanation: Low dose inhaled corticosteroid is appropriate for asthma management.

questions.questionText: A 27 yr old female came with a compliant of fever of five days duration. She also has a history of recent dental procedure and a new heart murmur on examination. What is the most likely diagnosis of this pt?
questions.explanation: The presentation with fever, recent dental procedure (potential source of bacteremia), and a new heart murmur is most consistent with infective endocarditis. This combination of findings strongly suggests bacterial infection of the heart valves.

questions.questionText: A 66 yr old male came to a clinic for BP check up. His blood pressure reading is 160/100 mmHg on two separate occasions. What is the next step in management of this Pt.?
options: Start single PO anti hypertensive drug
Start combined PO anti hypertensive drug
Appoint him after two days for repeat measurement
Advise on lifestyle modification & send him home
questions.explanation: For a patient with confirmed hypertension (BP 160/100 mmHg on two occasions), starting a single antihypertensive medication is the appropriate next step according to treatment guidelines. Lifestyle modifications should be advised alongside medication.

questions.questionText: A 28 yr male came to an Em OPD with a compliant of shortness of breath of six days duration. What is the most likely diagnosis of the Pt.?
questions.explanation: The symptoms suggest severe pneumonia.

questions.questionText: A 36 yr old male came with compliant of watery diarrhea & vomiting of two days duration. On examination, he appears dehydrated with dry mucous membranes and decreased skin turgor. What is the most likely cause of the pts. current condition?
questions.explanation: The most likely cause of the patient's condition is gastrointestinal fluid loss from diarrhea and vomiting, which has led to dehydration. This is a direct consequence of the gastrointestinal symptoms rather than a separate underlying condition.

questions.questionText: A 35 yr old woman came with compliant of right side flank pain of one day duration. What is the next best step in the management of this pt?
questions.explanation: Starting IV antibiotics is appropriate for suspected pyelonephritis.

questions.questionText: A 40 yrs old male pt. presented with compliant of pain & swelling of the first toe of his right foot. What is the most likely clinical Dx?
questions.explanation: The presentation is consistent with acute gouty arthritis.

questions.questionText: A 19 yr old male pt presented with a compliant of easy fatigability associated with occasional fever for the past three weeks. What is the most likely clinical Dx?
questions.explanation: The symptoms suggest a hematologic malignancy.

questions.questionText: A 40yr old female pt. was admitted to a medical ward with a diagnosis of severe community acquired pneumonia five days back. What is the most appropriate time to start vasopressor medication for the pt?
options: Immediately after the first record of BP
When BP fails to improve after adequate IV fluid
questions.explanation: Vasopressors should be started when BP fails to improve after fluids.

questions.questionText: A 22 yr old female student tried to commit suicide & ingested a chemical. What is the next best step in the management of this pt?
questions.explanation: Decontamination with charcoal is appropriate for chemical ingestion.

questions.questionText: A 45 yr old male pt came with compliant of untreatable vomiting of ingested matter which was intermittently blood tinged of four months duration. What is the most likely electrolyte abnormality that this pt. could have?
questions.explanation: Hypokalemia and hypochloremia are common in persistent vomiting.

questions.questionText: A 38 yrs old female came with a compliant of right breast lump of one year duration which was gradually increasing in size. What is the most likely Dx of this pt?
questions.explanation: The presentation is consistent with breast cancer.

questions.questionText: A 32 yr old male came to the OPD after he sustained a cut injury to his hand while working on a construction at a workplace. What is the appropriate management for the pt?
questions.explanation: For a clean cut injury in a patient who likely has had previous tetanus immunization (32-year-old adult), tetanus anti-toxoid (TAT) alone is appropriate if the last dose was over 5 years ago. This active immunization boosts the existing antibody response. Tetanus immunoglobulin (TIG) is typically reserved for severely contaminated wounds or for patients with unknown or incomplete immunization history.

questions.questionText: A 20 yrs old male came to emergency OPD with compliant of abdominal pain, vomiting of ingested water & loss of appetite associated with low grade fever of two days duration. What is the most likely Dx of the pt?
questions.explanation: The symptoms suggest acute appendicitis.

questions.questionText: A 54 yr old female came with a compliant of abdominal pain of three days duration. What is the first line of management of this pt?
options: Start her on broad spectrum antibiotics
questions.explanation: Emergency surgery is indicated for acute abdomen.

questions.questionText: A 40 yr old male came with a compliant of bleeding just after defecation of three weeks duration. What is the most likely Dx of this pt?
questions.explanation: The symptoms are consistent with anal fissure.

questions.questionText: A 68 yrs old male presented with complaints of failure to pass urine and lower abdominal pain of 10 hours duration. What is the most appropriate initial step in the management of this pt?
questions.explanation: For acute urinary retention, transurethral catheterization is the standard first-line management. It's less invasive than suprapubic catheterization or needle aspiration and provides immediate relief. Condom catheters are not appropriate for retention. If transurethral catheterization fails, then suprapubic catheterization would be considered. Needle aspiration would only be a temporary emergency measure, not the first choice.

questions.questionText: An 18 yr old student came to a HC with compliant of pain in the groin and lower abdominal area of six hours duration. What is the most likely Dx for the pt?
questions.explanation: The presentation is consistent with testicular torsion, which typically presents with acute onset of severe groin and lower abdominal pain in young males. This is a urological emergency requiring immediate intervention.

questions.questionText: A 10yr old male presented to a HC with a compliant of severe pain over the right forearm after he sustained falling down accident from a two meter height. What is the appropriate initial step in the mgt of the pt?
questions.explanation: Applying a posterior slab is appropriate for forearm fractures.

questions.questionText: A 12 yrs old male presented to a hospital with a compliant of severe pain over the right side of his pelvic which is not relieved by strong analgesics of five months duration. What is the most likely Dx?
questions.explanation: The symptoms suggest a chondrosarcoma.

questions.questionText: A 35 yrs old male came with compliant of fast breathing and chest tightness after he fell down from the second floor to a stony ground on his chest. What is the next step in the management of this pt?
options: Insert a chest tube & put him on oxygen
Put him on oxygen & order chest x-ray
Do needle thoracentesis at 2nd intercostals space
questions.explanation: With rapid breathing and chest tightness after significant chest trauma, tension pneumothorax should be suspected, which is a life-threatening emergency. Needle thoracentesis at the 2nd intercostal space provides immediate decompression to relieve tension pneumothorax. This is a time-sensitive intervention that shouldn't be delayed for imaging studies or hospital referral when clinical signs strongly suggest tension pneumothorax.

questions.questionText: A 4 year old male child was presented immediately after he sustained electrical burn injury to his arm. What is the most common complication this pt can develop?
questions.explanation: Compartment syndrome is the most immediate life-threatening complication of electrical burns to an extremity. The electrical current causes deep tissue damage, swelling, and increased pressure within the fascial compartment, which can compromise blood flow and nerve function. This requires emergency intervention including potential fasciotomy to prevent permanent tissue damage and loss of limb function.

questions.questionText: A 50 yr old male came with a compliant of left leg swelling of six months duration which worsens upon standing & long distance walking. What is the appropriate initiated management for this pt?
options: Encourage him to stay in supine position for longer hours
Advise him to use elastic bandage on daytime
Refer him to a specialist directly
questions.explanation: Using elastic bandages can help manage venous insufficiency.

questions.questionText: An 18 month old child brought with a compliant of intractable vomiting of ingested matter & discomfort in his neck since two days ago. What is the most likely Dx of this child?
questions.explanation: The symptoms suggest foreign body aspiration.

questions.questionText: A three week infant born at 32 weeks of gestation & weighing 1750g, was brought to OPD with compliant of abdominal distension, feeding intolerance, and vomiting. What is the most appropriate immediate step in the management of the infant?
questions.explanation: NPO with IV fluids is appropriate for suspected necrotizing enterocolitis.

questions.questionText: A four day infant, delivered at home, was presented with complaints of irritability & difficulty in opening of the mouth associated with hunger & crying. What measure could have prevented this condition from occurring?
options: Active immunization of the neonate with DPT
questions.explanation: Maternal immunization with tetanus toxoid could have prevented neonatal tetanus.

questions.questionText: A neonate born to a diabetic mother, was brought to the clinic with irritability & jitteriness. What is the most likely explanation for this condition?
questions.explanation: Hypoglycemia is the most common metabolic complication in infants of diabetic mothers. During pregnancy, maternal hyperglycemia leads to fetal hyperinsulinemia. After birth, when the maternal glucose supply is cut off, the infant's high insulin levels continue, causing rapid glucose utilization and resulting in hypoglycemia. Clinical signs include irritability, jitteriness, tremors, seizures, and in severe cases, loss of consciousness.

questions.questionText: A one year old infant was brought to the clinic with compliant of low grade fever and runny nose followed by paroxysm of whooping cough of two weeks duration. What vaccine could have prevented this condition?
questions.explanation: DPT vaccine prevents whooping cough.

questions.questionText: A mother brought her two yr old child with complaints of coryza, cough, conjunctivitis, and fever. What is the most likely Dx?
questions.explanation: The symptoms are consistent with measles.

questions.questionText: A five yr old boy was brought to HC after having watery diarrhea of one day duration. What is the most appropriate initial management for the pt?
options: Give fluid & food to treat diarrhea at home
Give fluid & food for some dehydration
questions.explanation: Fluid and food for some dehydration is appropriate.

questions.questionText: A four yr old girl was brought to a HC with complaints of cough, fever, & shortness of breath of two weeks duration. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The symptoms suggest presumptive tuberculosis.

questions.questionText: An eight yr old child came to an OPD complaining of intermittent fever of one day duration. What is the most prevalent severity sign in this child?
questions.explanation: Jaundice is a significant finding in this context.

questions.questionText: A five yr old child was presented with a compliant of foul smelling diarrhea associated with crampy abdominal pain, bloating of three weeks duration. What is the most appropriate first line drug for this case?
questions.explanation: Metronidazole is the first-line treatment for giardiasis or amoebiasis, which commonly present with foul-smelling diarrhea, crampy abdominal pain, and bloating. The prolonged duration (three weeks) suggests a parasitic infection rather than a viral cause. Metronidazole is effective against anaerobic organisms and intestinal protozoa like Giardia lamblia and Entamoeba histolytica.

questions.questionText: A seven yr old child has easy fatigability, dyspnea, & body swelling. What is the most likely precipitant of the heart failure in the child?
questions.explanation: Severe anemia can precipitate heart failure in children.

questions.questionText: A seven yr old child came with a referral from another Hospital. What is the most appropriate next step in the pt's care?
options: Follow up with weekly Benzathine penicillin
Follow up with monthly Benzathine penicillin
Follow up with single dose of Benzathine penicillin
questions.explanation: Monthly Benzathine penicillin is appropriate for rheumatic fever prophylaxis.

questions.questionText: A four yr old child was presented with compliant of barking cough, hoarseness of voice & inspiratory strider. What is the initial Rx for this child?
questions.explanation: Dexamethasone is the initial treatment for croup.

questions.questionText: A 10 month old boy was brought to an emergency OPD after having abnormal body movement which is characterized by flexion & extension of extremities. What is most appropriate next step in the management of this child?
questions.explanation: Diazepam is the most appropriate immediate management for active seizures in a child. It acts rapidly to stop seizure activity. In an emergency setting, controlling the seizure is the priority before determining if long-term antiepileptic drugs are needed. After stabilization, further workup should be done to determine the underlying cause (febrile seizure, epilepsy, infection, etc.).

questions.questionText: A 12 month old infant, who was on formula feeding since one month, was brought to the OPD for routine checkup. What is the most likely explanation for this finding?
questions.explanation: Iron deficiency anemia is the most likely explanation. Formula-fed infants after 6 months of age are at higher risk of iron deficiency unless they receive iron-fortified formula or complementary foods rich in iron. The rapid growth rate and insufficient iron stores from birth make infants particularly vulnerable to iron deficiency anemia.

questions.questionText: A four yr old child was presented with compliant of vomiting & diarrhea of three days duration. What is the most likely Dx?
questions.explanation: The presence of edema suggests kwashiorkor.

questions.questionText: A 5 yr old male child who was admitted in the ward & being treated for severe acute malnutrition (marasmus) for the past one week, currently developed profuse watery diarrhea of 12 hours duration. What is the most appropriate next step in the management of this child?
options: ResoMal 10 ml/kg over the first hour
RL 3ml/kg in 30 minutes for two hours
questions.explanation: Rapid rehydration is critical in this scenario.

questions.questionText: A 15 yr old child came to an OPD for regular checkup. The child has a history of polyuria, polydipsia, and weight loss over the past month. Random blood glucose is 280 mg/dl. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The presentation with classic symptoms of diabetes (polyuria, polydipsia, weight loss) and elevated blood glucose in a 15-year-old is most consistent with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus. Type 1 diabetes typically presents in children and adolescents with these acute symptoms.

questions.questionText: A seven year old girl who is known diabetic pt. & is on Insulin, presented with complaints of abdominal pain & vomiting of two days duration. What is the most appropriate next step in the management of the pt?
questions.explanation: For a diabetic child with abdominal pain and vomiting who cannot take oral nutrition, adding 5% dextrose to IV fluids is essential to prevent hypoglycemia while continuing insulin therapy. Diabetic patients require both insulin and glucose, especially during illness. Discontinuing insulin or significantly changing the regimen during illness can lead to diabetic ketoacidosis, while failing to provide glucose can lead to hypoglycemia.

questions.questionText: A 32 yr old G-II mother came to the ANC clinic for first visit with complaints of severe nausea & persistent vomiting. What is the most appropriate advice for the mother?
options: Advise her that this condition is treatable
Advise her on complications of abortion
Advise her to use ginger and spicy foods
Advise her on the line of termination
questions.explanation: This condition is treatable and can be managed.

questions.questionText: A 24 yr old G-III, P-I, A-I mother, whose LNMP is not known but claims to be amenorrhic for the past one & half months, came to the HC with complaints of vaginal bleeding & severe lower abdominal pain of two days duration. What is the most appropriate next step in the management of her condition?
questions.explanation: Serum Beta HCG is necessary to assess for pregnancy complications.

questions.questionText: A 28 year old G-III, P-II mother came to a HC for the first ANC visit. What is the most appropriate management of the pt?
questions.explanation: Continuing the same ART regimen is appropriate.

questions.questionText: A 32 yr old G-IV, P-III mother presented to an emergency OPD at 38 weeks of gestation with a complaint of bright red & painless vaginal bleeding of two days duration. What is the next step in the management of the mother?
options: Admit her & prepare for elective CS
Start induction of labor with oxytocin
questions.explanation: Elective cesarean section is indicated for placenta previa.

questions.questionText: A 26 yrs old G-III, P-II mother presented with a pushing down pain of six hours duration on a gestational stage of 39 wks. What is the most likely Dx?
questions.explanation: The symptoms suggest cord prolapse.

questions.questionText: A 23 yrs old G-I woman presented to the labor ward at active first stage of labor at 40 weeks of gestation. What is the most appropriate next step in the pt's care?
options: Put the woman in knee-chest position
questions.explanation: Amniotomy is appropriate to manage labor.

questions.questionText: A 24 yr old G-I woman who is at gestational age of 40 wks was started on induction of labor for gestational hypertension. What is the most likely cause for the pt's problem?
questions.explanation: Uterine atony is a common cause of postpartum hemorrhage.

questions.questionText: A 59 yr old P-II mother came to a clinic with a complaint of increased abdominal girth associated with bloating, early satiety and urinary frequency of six months duration. What is the primary factor determining the prognosis of the pt?
questions.explanation: The stage of the disease is crucial for prognosis.

questions.questionText: A 23 yr old single woman came to for a clinic for consultation about her reproductive health status. What is the next recommended PAP smear screening schedule for the woman?
questions.explanation: PAP smear screening is recommended every three years.

questions.questionText: A 47 yrs old P-VI mother presented to a HC with a complaint of pelvic pressure and feeling of incomplete emptying of the bladder associated with low back pain of four years duration. What is the most likely Dx?
questions.explanation: The symptoms suggest uterovaginal prolapse.

questions.questionText: A five yr old child was brought to pediatric OPD with a complaint of ear pain and low grade intermittent fever of four days duration. What is the next step in the management of the pt?
options: Admit and treat with IV antibiotics
Advice to ear wash twice daily
questions.explanation: Oral antibiotics are indicated for acute otitis media.

questions.questionText: A four yr old girl has visited different health facilities with a complaint of frequent tonsillitis and was treated with oral antibiotics. What condition is the child at great risk?
questions.explanation: Obstructive sleep apnea is a risk due to enlarged tonsils.

questions.questionText: A 38 yr old male presented with diffuse submandibular swelling associated with fever and throat pain of one week duration. What type of antibiotics should be considered?
questions.explanation: Antibiotics should cover both aerobes and anaerobes.

questions.questionText: A 25 yr old man came complaining of plaque accumulation on his lower arch and bleeding with slight touch to his gingival area. What is the effective long term control method for this case?
questions.explanation: Scaling is essential for long-term control of plaque.

questions.questionText: A 28-year-old male presented with postoperative pain after extraction of right lower side molar tooth was done five days back. What is the most likely Dx of the pt?
questions.explanation: The symptoms suggest alveolar osteitis (dry socket).

questions.questionText: A 30-year-old woman came with a complaint of a short, sharp and shock type of tooth pain which gets exacerbated during tooth brushing of two weeks duration. What is the most likely diagnosis for this case?
questions.explanation: Dentinal sensitivity is likely due to exposed dentin.

questions.questionText: A patient with avulsed primary central incisors after he sustained an accident an hour back came to the hospital. What is the most effective management for the patient?
questions.explanation: For avulsed primary (deciduous) teeth, reassurance and sending home is the appropriate management. Unlike permanent teeth, primary teeth are generally not reimplanted after avulsion because reimplantation can damage the developing permanent tooth buds underneath. Management includes pain control, soft diet recommendations, and monitoring for possible complications. Only permanent teeth are candidates for replacement and fixation.

questions.questionText: A 46-year-old man came to the clinic for check up. During the visit, he expresses feelings of hopelessness, mentions having a specific plan to end his life, and reports a previous suicide attempt two years ago. He has been drinking heavily and has no family support. What is the suicide risk level of this patient?
questions.explanation: This patient demonstrates multiple high-risk factors for suicide: previous suicide attempt, specific suicide plan, feelings of hopelessness, substance abuse (alcohol), and lack of social support. These factors indicate high suicide risk, warranting immediate intervention including possible hospitalization and close monitoring.

questions.questionText: A 32-year-old female patient presented with hallucination, delusion and disorganized speech for the last seven months. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The symptoms are consistent with schizophrenia.

questions.questionText: A 32-year-old man came with a complaint of painless mass on the right upper eyelid of three month duration. What is the most likely clinical diagnosis of the patient?
questions.explanation: The presentation is consistent with a chalazion.

questions.questionText: A 34-year-old male patient came with complaints of pain and blurring of vision on his left eye of three days duration after he sustained a falling down accident. What is the most appropriate initial step in the management of the patient?
options: Admit and start him on IV antibiotics
Send him home with oral antibiotics
Admit and start him on eye drops
questions.explanation: Referral to an ophthalmologist is necessary for eye trauma.

questions.questionText: A 35-year-old female presented with sudden onset left eye pain and blurring of vision of three hours duration which is associated with severe headache and photophobia. What is the most likely diagnosis of the patient?
questions.explanation: The symptoms suggest angle closure glaucoma.

questions.questionText: A four-year-old child was brought by her parents with a complaint of whitish central spot on both eyes of one week duration. What is the most appropriate initial management for the child?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A supplementation is crucial for corneal health.

questions.questionText: A 50-year-old male patient with Parkinson's disease came with a complaint of skin lesion of three months duration. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Seborrheic dermatitis is common in Parkinson's disease.

questions.questionText: A 15-year-old girl came with asymptomatic skin lesion of one year duration. What is the most appropriate Rx for this stage of the disease?
questions.explanation: Topical retinoids are effective for acne management.

questions.questionText: A known RVI pt. who has been on HAART for the past six months, came with a complaint of fever, chills and generalized reddening of the skin of five days duration. What drug is the most likely cause of the pt's condition?
questions.explanation: Nevirapine is associated with skin reactions.

questions.questionText: A 23-year-old housewife came with a complaint of pruritic skin lesion of three weeks duration. What is the most likely Dx of this pt?
questions.explanation: The symptoms suggest scabies.

questions.questionText: A number of pts are waiting for their turn in line to be seen by a health professional. What ethical principle does the health professional implement?
questions.explanation: Justice refers to fairness in the distribution of healthcare.

questions.questionText: A 35 yr old man came to a hospital with complaint of recurrent headache of two weeks duration. What quality of compassionate care is violated in this care?
questions.explanation: Empathy is crucial in patient-provider interactions.

questions.questionText: A health care professional, who has been working in emergency department for the past two years, started to come late to work. What is the most likely cause of his behavioral change?
questions.explanation: Burnout is common in high-stress healthcare environments.

questions.questionText: A pt came to a HC for treatment. What is the most appropriate principle to be followed in managing the pt?
questions.explanation: Recognizing diversity is essential in patient care.

questions.questionText: A 28 yr old depressed male pt came for a psychiatric evaluation. What is the most likely reason for using empathic statement during the interview?
options: To help the pt to disclose himself
To help the pt to feel being understood
To help the provider to lead the interview
To help the provider to get more information
questions.explanation: Empathy helps build rapport and encourages disclosure.

questions.questionText: A health professional, who is working in a referral hospital, also works in a private diagnostic center which he owns. What is the best recommendation to reduce the conflict in this case?
questions.explanation: Disclosure of affiliations helps manage conflicts of interest.

questions.questionText: A health professional uses an open-ended question at first and close-ended question in the middle of an interview. What is the evidence that understanding is established in the case?
options: Interview technique of the health professional
Dx and Rx alternative is communicated
Decision on the treatment plan is made collaboratively
questions.explanation: Collaborative decision-making indicates mutual understanding.

questions.questionText: A physician who has examining a 48 yr old female pt, reached at a Dx with a poor prognosis. What is the most likely issue that should be considered in disclosing the Dx?
options: One's ability to accept the pt's reaction
questions.explanation: Psychological issues are critical when disclosing bad news.

questions.questionText: A public health officer, who is interviewing pts, uses a separate folder to record cocky pt's history and all records related to his pts. What is the primary reason that the health professional tries to maintain confidentiality?
questions.explanation: Maintaining confidentiality promotes trust in the patient-provider relationship.

questions.questionText: In an outpatient clinic with a very crowded waiting area, a health professional was giving seat and telling pts to wait until he calls their name. What professional moral value explains the health professional's judgment?
options: Giving attention to pt is good
Considering what pts say is helpful
Pts have the right to be aggressive
Treating pt with consideration is good
questions.explanation: Treating patients with consideration is a fundamental ethical principle that encompasses respect for patient dignity and welfare. In this scenario, the health professional is demonstrating consideration by managing a crowded waiting area in an orderly way, ensuring each patient will be seen in turn, and showing respect for those who may need seating more than others. This reflects the ethical principle of beneficence (acting in the best interest of patients) and respect for persons.

questions.questionText: The number of cancer pts & related deaths is increasing worldwide. What is the most appropriate research type for this scenario?
questions.explanation: Applied research is necessary to develop effective treatments.

questions.questionText: A researcher has traced published & unpublished literatures related to his research area. What is the most likely violated literature review criterion in this scenario?
questions.explanation: The literature review must be up-to-date to reflect current knowledge.

questions.questionText: Investigators wanted to assess the effect of school-based iron supplementation on cognitive development. What is the most appropriate study design for the above scenario?
questions.explanation: An experimental design is appropriate for assessing intervention effects.

questions.questionText: A research institution wants to identify the type of cardiovascular morbidity in a community. What is the most appropriate sampling method used in this scenario?
questions.explanation: Cluster random sampling is effective for community studies.

questions.questionText: A hospital manager wishes to know what proportions of pts admitted to the orthopedic department has died. What is the sample size needed for the above study?
questions.explanation: The sample size of 171 would be appropriate for estimating a proportion with reasonable precision. Sample size calculations for proportion studies depend on several factors: expected proportion (mortality rate), desired confidence level (typically 95%), and acceptable margin of error. Without knowing these specific parameters, 171 represents a reasonable sample size that balances statistical power with feasibility for a hospital department study on mortality rates.

questions.questionText: An epidemiologist has planned to estimate the prevalence of sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS) among infants admitted to the ICU of a hospital. What is the most appropriate measurement tool to be used?
questions.explanation: Document review is appropriate for prevalence studies.

questions.questionText: The Ethiopian medical journal reported a study of 13 HIV positive pts, who were treated with HAART for at least six months. What is the Inter Quartile Range (IQR) for this data set?
questions.explanation: IQR is calculated from the quartiles of the data set.

questions.questionText: Hemoglobin AIC is a serum measure often used to monitor compliance among diabetic pts. What is the most appropriate measure of variation for this sample?
questions.explanation: Standard deviation is the most appropriate measure of variation for HbA1c values. HbA1c is typically normally distributed in a population, making standard deviation ideal for quantifying the spread of values. It provides a reliable measure of how much individual HbA1c values deviate from the mean, which is valuable for assessing glycemic control variation across a diabetic population.

questions.questionText: Cardiovascular risk factors such as diastolic blood pressure (mmHg) and HDL cholesterol levels (mg/dl) were measured among children in every 3 year intervals. What is the correct statement about the above scenario?
options: The variability in cholesterol level measurements and BP cannot be compared
There is high variability in cholesterol level measurements than blood pressure
There is high variability in blood pressure measurements than cholesterol
There is consistency of measurements in cholesterol level than blood pressure
questions.explanation: The variability in cholesterol level measurements and blood pressure cannot be compared directly because they have different units of measurement (mg/dl vs mmHg) and different biological ranges. To properly compare variability between these different measures, one would need to use standardized measures like coefficient of variation, which accounts for the different scales of measurement.

questions.questionText: A study was conducted among 18 male and 11 female hypertensive pts to measure tire serum creatinine concentration level. What is the 95% confidence interval of mean difference?
questions.explanation: The 95% confidence interval of 0.89 to 2.51 indicates that the true mean difference in serum creatinine between males and females lies within this range with 95% confidence. Since this interval doesn't include zero, there is a statistically significant difference between the groups. Males typically have higher creatinine levels than females due to greater muscle mass, which is reflected in this confidence interval showing a positive difference.

questions.questionText: A group of researchers planned to conduct a study on Alzheimer's pts. What is the most appropriate statistics for this scenario?
questions.explanation: Chi-square test is appropriate for categorical data comparisons.

questions.questionText: A group of researchers want to examine the association between ANC service utilization and birth outcome. What is the value of relative risk for this scenario?
questions.explanation: Relative risk indicates the strength of association between ANC utilization and outcomes.

title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Sociology (2016)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Sociology (2016). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about the pre-industrial cities?
options: Dependence on animate source of energy for the production of goods and services (hammers, pulleys, wheels)
Efficient methods of food preservation and storage.
High specialization of work like handicrafts work
The amount of surplus food has been limited by mechanized agriculture
questions.explanation: Pre-industrial cities relied on animate sources of energy for production.

questions.questionText: If the aim of the research is single-time description (political attitude at one time), which survey is most appropriate?
options: Cross-sectional Survey is the most appropriate
Trend and Cohort Studies are most appropriate
questions.explanation: A cross-sectional survey is designed for single-time descriptions.

questions.questionText: ____ is a system of authority, which is based on a rational calculation of advantages; i.e., it is based on rationally produced laws, norms and leaders are appointed or elected through legal procedures.
questions.explanation: In Weber's typology of authority, Rational-Legal Authority is based on a system of rules and procedures that are rationally established. Leaders derive their legitimacy from these established rules rather than from tradition or personal qualities. This type of authority is characteristic of modern bureaucratic states and organizations.

questions.questionText: Among the various levels of measurement, which one is appropriate to illustrate class categories as low, medium, and high?
questions.explanation: Ordinal levels of measurement are used for ranking categories.

questions.questionText: Virtual population analysis enables the scientist to predict the future catches.
questions.explanation: Modeling is used for predicting future outcomes in virtual population analysis.

questions.questionText: From the following which one is not the advantage of political sociology?
options: Political sociology tries to link politics with the general theories of society.
It studies power as distributed in some relationships in society, only embodied in the formal governmental structures
It allows the examination of the variety of structures and institutions that might otherwise be missed - politics in private organizations, in the family, in working places.
It tries to have a holistic approach.
questions.explanation: Political sociology examines power beyond just formal governmental structures.

questions.questionText: Economic aid has largely failed to promote modernization in developing countries because:
options: There are no clearly defined projects into which the money can be directed
The United Nations has refused to call on rich countries to provide it
Debt repayments with interest can be greater than the amount of money received
Rich countries are unwilling to provide sufficient aid
questions.explanation: High debt repayments with interest often exceed the original aid amount, creating a debt cycle that hinders development rather than promoting it. This is a key critique of international aid programs.

questions.questionText: According to the constructionist perspective, all of the following are sound expressions regarding the formation of ethnic identity except.
options: Ethnicity is acquired; it is not inborn.
questions.explanation: The constructionist perspective views ethnicity as socially constructed rather than biologically determined. It argues that ethnic identities are created, maintained, and modified through social interaction and historical processes, not innate or inherited traits. Therefore, describing ethnicity as 'an innate phenomenon' contradicts the constructionist view, which emphasizes ethnicity as learned, fluid, and contextual.

questions.questionText: All of the following are the basic assumptions in defining social problems Except
options: They have objective and subjective dimensions
questions.explanation: The option 'None' is not a basic assumption in defining social problems. The other three options correctly list key characteristics: harmful nature, social origins, and having both objective conditions and subjective perceptions.

questions.questionText: Identify the incorrect expression concerning social policy from the following.
options: Social policy has a linkage with nation-building.
Social policy is always a force for good.
Social policy aims at fostering community well-being.
questions.explanation: Social policy can have both positive and negative effects.

questions.questionText: A theoretical format that helps for a diagrammatic representation of social events is called ___
questions.explanation: Modeling provides a visual representation of social events.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about the view of Karl Marx and Max Weber on the notion of social class?
options: They viewed social class as a source of social equality.
They both thought that the only factor influencing class formation was the economy.
They focused on the material aspect of the social class formation.
They viewed social class as a desirable social phenomenon.
questions.explanation: Marx and Weber focused on material conditions in class formation.

questions.questionText: Distinguish which of the following statements best describes the consequence of social problems?
options: Creation of job opportunities in reaction to the problems.
decline in mental health issues and disorders.
Strengthen social cohesion and social capital.
questions.explanation: Social problems often lead to disorganization and disintegration.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about the state of crime in Ethiopia?
options: Males are less criminal than females
Imprisonment is the most common type of punishment
Life imprisonment over-weights all other types of punishment
Capital punishment over-weights all other types of punishment
questions.explanation: Imprisonment is the prevalent form of punishment in Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: Terminal and ex-post evaluation is often conducted by ____________
questions.explanation: Ex-post evaluators assess outcomes after implementation.

questions.questionText: _______ is the study of the interactions between human and non-human nature in different cultures.
questions.explanation: Urban Ecology studies the interactions between humans and their environment.

questions.questionText: _______ Management is the process by which a product is sourced from an external supplier.
questions.explanation: Procurement management involves sourcing products externally.

questions.questionText: From the following, which one is False about Ceasar Lombroso's theory of born criminal?
options: Ancestral through back or hereditary as the main causes of crime
He compares the physical characteristics of criminals with Atavism, the early stage of human evolution
His theory gives attention to external factors like the environment shaping criminal behavior
He forwarded the argument that a born criminal has peculiar body characteristics that differ from normal people
questions.explanation: Lombroso's biological theory of criminality emphasized innate, biological factors rather than environmental influences. His theory of the 'born criminal' argued that criminals were evolutionary throwbacks (atavism) identifiable by physical anomalies. The statement claiming 'his theory gives attention to external factors like the environment' is incorrect because Lombroso specifically attributed criminal behavior to biological determinism, not environmental factors.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the correct expression about the positive impact of globalization on national or ethnic identity?
options: Globalization has aggravated the role of national identity.
questions.explanation: Globalization can enhance cultural plurality.

questions.questionText: According to Weber _____ meant the probability that an event will be followed or accompanied by another event.
questions.explanation: Weber defined causality as the probability relationship between events. This concept was central to his methodology of understanding social phenomena through cause and effect relationships, while distinguishing between correlation and causation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a possible cause of social problems?
questions.explanation: Education is generally seen as a solution, not a cause of social problems.

questions.questionText: Urban sociology examines a great deal of issues except
options: History of urbanization to provide multiple perspectives
It does not emphasize on Physical aspects of urban contexts
The nature of and solutions to urban social problems
questions.explanation: Urban sociology does consider physical aspects of urban contexts.

questions.questionText: Identify the right sequence from the broadest to the narrowest in terms of their scope.
questions.explanation: Policies are broader than programs, which are broader than projects.

questions.questionText: ______ is a doctrine that assumes some groups always get the upper hand and rule the masses.
questions.explanation: Elitism refers to the idea that a small group holds power over the majority.

questions.questionText: ___________ the process through which religion's influence on other social institutions diminishes is:
questions.explanation: Secularization refers to the diminishing influence of religion.

questions.questionText: According to ____________ cities tended to grow in wedge-shaped patterns -- or sectors -- emanating from the central business district and centered on major transportation routes.
questions.explanation: The Sector Model describes urban growth in wedge-shaped patterns.

questions.questionText: The objective of crime measurement includes all except,
options: It is important to test, refine, and refute theories of crime causation
It enriches people's knowledge regarding attributes of crime and their current trend
It gives much attention to knowing trivial things to deal with crime and criminal behavior
It enables criminal justice agencies and other concerned bodies to plan for their future activities
questions.explanation: Crime measurement focuses on significant aspects, not trivialities.

questions.questionText: From the following which one is the central theme of the elite theory of political process?
options: The elite theory lays the conception that a society is divided into two groups and there are minorities or elite groups who rule the society and make decisions in a society.
The minority (the elite) is subordinate to the majority (the mass) because of its highly disorganized system of communication involving superior individuals.
The theory doesn't accept the existence of a single superior group, an elite group that monopolizes power in society.
It sees power as politically fragmented or diffused among the different sectors of society.
questions.explanation: The elite theory posits that a small group holds power over the majority.

questions.questionText: All of the following hold correct expressions of nationalism except.
options: It is an ideological movement aimed at maintaining the identity and unity of a nation.
It has something to do with state building and consolidation.
It may lead to the state collapse through bloody war.
Nationalism always remains ideological rather than appearing in the form of action.
questions.explanation: Nationalism can manifest in both ideology and action.

questions.questionText: _______ emphasis on the individual's interpretation of a situation and the importance of subjective meaning, was influential in the emergence of symbolic interactionism.
questions.explanation: Verstehen (German for 'understanding') is Weber's concept emphasizing the interpretive understanding of social action through empathically grasping the actor's subjective meanings. This approach, which focuses on how individuals interpret their social world, was influential in the development of symbolic interactionism, a perspective that examines how people create shared meanings through social interaction and interpretation of symbols.

questions.questionText: ___ argues that the logic and methods of the natural sciences are inappropriate in sociological theorizing and research because the subject matter of sociology is different from the subject matter of natural sciences.
questions.explanation: Interpretivism (also called anti-positivism) is an approach that argues that social sciences require different methods than natural sciences because human behavior involves meaning, intention, and interpretation. Unlike positivism, which advocates applying natural science methods to study society, interpretivism emphasizes understanding (verstehen) social action through the meanings actors attach to their behaviors rather than explaining causal relationships.

questions.questionText: All of the following are correct about primitive law Except:
options: It is the law of the pre-literate societies to resolve the daily problems of their members.
The law is handled not by religious persons or traditional shamans.
It is the law of the primitive societies before the emergence of the feudal system.
It is based on primitive cultural customs that are characterized by the lack of formal legal institutions or organization.
questions.explanation: In primitive law systems, legal matters were typically handled BY religious persons or traditional shamans, not separate from them. The statement that 'the law is handled not by religious persons or traditional shamans' is incorrect, as religious and traditional authorities were often central to primitive legal processes.

questions.questionText: Mr. X had governed Ethiopia for 35 years and the people highly believed that he would govern us again. The above descriptions qualify _____type of authority.
questions.explanation: Traditional authority is based on long-standing customs and beliefs.

questions.questionText: Anti-Apartheid Movement, Green Peace, Anti-Smoking Movement, and Anti-HIV Movement are an example of ______ groups.
questions.explanation: Promotional groups are social movements that actively advocate for specific causes or social changes rather than defending existing privileges or rights. These movements (Anti-Apartheid, Greenpeace, Anti-Smoking, Anti-HIV) all seek to promote particular social values, policies, or behavioral changes in society, distinguishing them from protective or defensive groups that primarily aim to preserve existing benefits or rights.

questions.questionText: _________ a stage in which people look for regularities or invariable social and natural laws through empirical research and theory.
questions.explanation: The Positive stage focuses on empirical research and laws.

questions.questionText: ____ refers to a kind of intellectual thinking in sociological theory that is distinct from contemporary sociological theory.
questions.explanation: Postmodern social theory represents a distinct approach that challenges the assumptions of modern sociological theory. It questions grand narratives, emphasizes plurality and diversity of perspectives, rejects universal truth claims, and focuses on deconstruction of traditional concepts.

questions.questionText: ______Plan provides a detailed description of the products (i.e., goods and services) to be procured from suppliers, the justification for procuring each product externally, and the schedule for procurement.
questions.explanation: A Procurement Plan outlines the details of sourcing products.

questions.questionText: Constitutional integrationist view of biological makeup as the main cause of crime includes all of the following factors, except.
questions.explanation: Gender is not typically viewed as a biological factor in this context.

questions.questionText: ___________ of a social problem comes from acknowledging that a particular social condition does negatively impact human lives.
questions.explanation: Objective reality refers to the acknowledgment of negative impacts.

questions.questionText: Systemic model examines the relationships between community attachment with all except
questions.explanation: The answer is 'None' because the systemic model of community attachment examines all of the other factors listed: length of residence, social position, and stage of life as determinants of community attachment.

questions.questionText: _______ are the overall results of project activities intended to achieve the immediate objectives.
questions.explanation: Outputs are the results of project activities.

questions.questionText: All of the following are the criteria applied in the policy formulation would then be measured in terms. Except
questions.explanation: The option 'None' is not a criterion used in policy formulation measurement. The other three options (Effectiveness, Efficiency, and Adequacy) are established criteria used to evaluate policy alternatives during formulation.

questions.questionText: ____ sees and understands social reality from the relationship between an individual's unique consciousness and the inter-subjective or shared consciousness that develops among people who share the same social world.
questions.explanation: Ethnomethodology, developed by Harold Garfinkel, examines how people make sense of their everyday social world through shared social practices. It focuses on the methods individuals use to construct their social reality and how common understandings emerge through interactions.

questions.questionText: Which phase of the policy-making process is marked by setting objectives?
questions.explanation: Policy formulation involves setting objectives.

questions.questionText: The process whereby the researcher specifies empirical observations that may be taken as indicators of the attributes contained within a given concept is called______________.
questions.explanation: Operationalization defines how concepts will be measured.

questions.questionText: Sociological theory, which argues that social problems arise from fundamental faults in the structure of a society and both reflect and reinforce inequalities based on social class, race, gender, and other dimensions, is called_____________.
questions.explanation: Conflict Theory focuses on structural inequalities.

questions.questionText: _________ are workers who sell their labor and who do not own their own means of production.
questions.explanation: Proletariats refer to the working class who sell their labor.

questions.questionText: ________ is best known in contemporary sociology for his contributions to our understanding of the patterns, or forms, of social interaction.
questions.explanation: Georg Simmel is recognized for his work on social interaction.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is Not among Non-probability sampling methods?
questions.explanation: Random Sampling is a probability sampling method.

questions.questionText: All of the following are the essential features of the classical tradition except
questions.explanation: The option 'None' is not a feature of classical sociological tradition. The other three options correctly identify key characteristics of classical theory: grand narratives (comprehensive explanations), universal assumptions, and focus on social change theories.

questions.questionText: ______ is defined as a method in philosophy that begins with the individual and his own conscious experience and tries to avoid prior assumptions, prejudices, and philosophical dogmas.
questions.explanation: Phenomenology, associated with Edmund Husserl and Alfred Schutz in sociology, is a philosophical approach that examines subjective experience by setting aside preconceptions to understand phenomena as they appear to consciousness. It focuses on how individuals perceive and make sense of their lived experiences.

questions.questionText: Erving Goffman celebrated study of behavior in a mental asylum, Asylums: Essays on the Social Situation of Mental Patients and Other Inmates in 1961 was the best example of ______ research in sociology.
questions.explanation: Goffman's work is a classic example of field research.

questions.questionText: _______ denotes those issues on which the government and its institutions feel compelled to act (e.g., the approval of treaties, or government departmental budget requests).
questions.explanation: The governmental agenda includes issues requiring government action.

questions.questionText: All of the following are the features of monitoring except?
questions.explanation: The option 'C&B' (Cost & Benefit) is not a standard feature of monitoring. Monitoring typically involves assessing intermediate results, attributes/indicators, and multi-level results throughout a project's implementation, but cost-benefit analysis is typically part of evaluation rather than monitoring.

questions.questionText: ______ is the international transfer of capital, goods, or services from a country or international organization for the benefit of the recipient country or its population.
questions.explanation: Foreign Aid refers to international assistance for development.

questions.questionText: _____ considered the law as an ideology of the ruling class that conceals the existing class division and inequality in society and exploitation of the labor class.
questions.explanation: Karl Marx viewed law as a tool of the ruling class.

questions.questionText: The best-known sociologist as a micro-sociologist who played a significant role in the development of small-group research is
questions.explanation: Georg Simmel is renowned for his pioneering work in micro-sociology, focusing on the forms and patterns of small-group interactions and social relationships. Unlike Marx, Weber, and Comte who primarily analyzed macro-level social structures and historical processes, Simmel examined dyads, triads, and small group dynamics, making fundamental contributions to understanding social interactions at the micro level.

questions.questionText: When researchers define the notion of self-esteem as positive or negative feelings towards oneself, it is called_______________.
questions.explanation: Operationalization defines how self-esteem is measured.

questions.questionText: ______ is a systematic evaluation of how effectively a policy addresses the targeted problem or issue, meets people's needs, and achieves its goals.
questions.explanation: Policy analysis evaluates the effectiveness of policies.

questions.questionText: It is extremely difficult to gather reliable statistics pertaining to the types, distribution, and frequency of crime and delinquency, because:
options: Most criminals fail to be discovered
Victims might be at criminal cases
questions.explanation: All listed factors contribute to the difficulty in gathering reliable crime statistics.

questions.questionText: Our_________ position is directly underpinning our theoretical perspective.
questions.explanation: Epistemological positions influence theoretical perspectives.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not true According to Differential Associations theory
options: Criminality is a normally learned behavior
The one who lives with a thief has a high probability of becoming a thief
Biological traits and drives play a crucial role in shaping human behavior
Criminal behavior is learned in interaction with other persons
questions.explanation: According to Sutherland's Differential Association theory, criminal behavior is learned through social interaction rather than being determined by biological factors. The theory specifically rejects biological determinism, emphasizing that criminal behavior is learned just like any other behavior through social processes and interactions.

questions.questionText: From the following which one is not the major concern area of the sociology of law:
options: Analyses of the social role of the criminal, lawyer, judge, and it did not relate to the general structure of the society.
The sociology of law is primarily concerned with how the formal norms of society (legal practices) and enforcing agents act towards each other and deviants and criminals.
Sociology of law has no relationship with political sociology a concern for the nature of legitimate authority and social control.
The sociology of law studies the laws governing the development of human society and the effects of legal provisions.
questions.explanation: The sociology of law does analyze the social roles of legal actors (criminals, lawyers, judges) AND relates these to the general structure of society. The statement claiming it 'did not relate to the general structure of society' is incorrect, as connecting legal institutions to broader social structures is a central concern of the sociology of law.

questions.questionText: All of the following are among the Factors to be taken into account in Planning. Except
options: Values, Interests, Beliefs, Ethics, and Slants (VIBES)
questions.explanation: Adoption of the plan is not a factor in planning.

questions.questionText: A design that studies the same people, events or activities over a time period is called_____________.
questions.explanation: Longitudinal studies track the same subjects over time.

questions.questionText: ____ asks if, is the project both advantageous and acceptable to the people affected by it.
questions.explanation: Social feasibility assesses the acceptability of a project.

questions.questionText: The capitalist world economy is what Wallerstein(1974) would call a 'world system'. This term refers to:
options: means of transporting money between different areas of a country
An empire with a bureaucratic administration but no political center
An awareness of risks and dangers that affect the environment as a whole
unit with a division of labor that extends across ethnic and cultural groups
questions.explanation: In Wallerstein's World-Systems Theory, a 'world system' refers to an integrated economic unit with a global division of labor that transcends political and cultural boundaries. It includes core, semi-peripheral and peripheral regions with different economic functions and power relations.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is different from the others?
questions.explanation: The option 'Has general objectives' is less specific than the others.

questions.questionText: All of the following are the distinguishing features of terminal evaluation except?
options: It undertakes a careful examination of performance
It takes a longer time to review the initial outputs and effects
questions.explanation: Terminal evaluation focuses on final outcomes, not intermediate results.

questions.questionText: Increases in real GNP per capita occur when
options: Government programs direct resources away from investment goods to consumer goods.
Tariffs and quotas prevent countries from trading and thus prevent dollars from leaving each country.
The rate of growth in real GNP is greater than the rate of growth in the population.
The level of consumption expenditures rises relative to the level of saving.
questions.explanation: Increases in real GNP per capita occur when economic growth outpaces population growth.

questions.questionText: ______ is the spread of worldwide practices, relations, consciousness, and organization of social life.
questions.explanation: Globalization refers to the interconnectedness of social practices and relations.

questions.questionText: ______ is the study of legal institutions of the society in light of sociological concepts, theories, and approaches.
questions.explanation: Sociology of law examines legal institutions through sociological lenses.

questions.questionText: All of the following are the factors for the coming of the welfare state and social policy EXCEPT
questions.explanation: The answer is 'None' because advancing industrialism, labor movements, and capitalist development are all recognized factors that contributed to the emergence of welfare states and social policies. The option 'None' is not a factor in this development.

questions.questionText: According to Durkheim Organic solidarity is
options: It is the characteristic of primitive society
Largely dominate common belief and custom
questions.explanation: Durkheim's concept of organic solidarity refers to social cohesion based on high social differentiation and interdependence created by division of labor in complex modern societies. Unlike mechanical solidarity (found in simpler societies), organic solidarity results from differences between individuals and their complementary functions.

questions.questionText: _____ is performed by persons who have a direct role in the program/project or mid-term evaluation can be done by the management team persons assigned from the implementing agency.
questions.explanation: Mid-term evaluation is conducted by those directly involved in the project.

questions.questionText: __________ assumes that effective social policy is built on the cornerstone of careful problem definition.
questions.explanation: The problem-centered approach emphasizes defining issues clearly.

questions.questionText: Classical criminology differs from positive criminology in that, classical criminology:
options: Emphasized on the criminal not the crime
Emphasized the actor not the action
Insisted punishment should fit the criminal
Emphasized on the crime not the criminal
questions.explanation: Classical criminology, associated with Cesare Beccaria and Jeremy Bentham, focused on the crime rather than the criminal, emphasizing free will, rational choice, and proportional punishment. In contrast, positive criminology (developed by Lombroso and others) focused on the criminal, viewing crime as determined by biological, psychological, or social factors beyond individual control. Classical criminology advocated that punishment should fit the crime, not be tailored to the criminal.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not a characteristic of urban urbanization
options: The urban community is a complex multi-group society.
Formal means of social control dominate such as law, legislation, police, and court
It is dominated by primary relations.
Urban society is heterogeneous and known for its diversity and complexity.
questions.explanation: Urban areas are characterized by secondary (formal, impersonal, specialized) rather than primary relations (intimate, personal, face-to-face). While rural communities typically feature strong primary relations and personal connections, urban environments are marked by more impersonal, contractual, and specialized relationships. This distinction was notably emphasized by sociologists like Tönnies (Gemeinschaft vs. Gesellschaft) and Durkheim (mechanical vs. organic solidarity).

questions.questionText: _____ is an initial review of project ideas and concepts to see if they should be advanced or abandoned at an early stage.
questions.explanation: Screening assesses project ideas for viability.

questions.questionText: All of the following are the requirements for studying social problems Except?
options: Evaluating the social norms and values
questions.explanation: Evaluating social norms and values is not a requirement for studying social problems.

questions.questionText: Delinquency differs from other forms of crime in that, delinquency is:
options: breach of minor laws by the young
Any offense against human life and property
Any offense against minor laws by an organized group of citizens
Any offense against conventional laws by youngsters
questions.explanation: Delinquency specifically refers to offenses committed by minors.

questions.questionText: __________ is seen as the process of change towards those types of social, economic, and political systems that have developed in Western Europe and North America.
questions.explanation: Modernization Theory views development as a linear process through which traditional societies progress toward becoming modern societies resembling Western industrialized nations. It emphasizes industrialization, urbanization, rationalization, and democratization as key processes, suggesting all societies follow similar paths of development.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is false about urbanization?
options: One necessary condition for urbanization was surplus products
Population growth is the only reason for urbanization.
The advancement of agricultural technology is a factor of urbanization.
questions.explanation: Population growth is not the only reason for urbanization.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is or are NOT among the Advantages of the Field-research Method?
options: It is the only method available when the researcher studies an unknown group to outsiders.
Field research provides much richer information about social life.
Field research gives the investigator more flexibility than other methods.
Different researchers can come up with differing descriptions of the same phenomenon.
questions.explanation: The challenge of different researchers potentially coming up with differing descriptions of the same phenomenon is actually a limitation of field research, not an advantage. This issue relates to concerns about reliability and researcher subjectivity in qualitative field research methods.

questions.questionText: According to Parsons, the relationship between two or more individuals who work with certain orientations or goals is known as_______
questions.explanation: Social action refers to interactions with shared goals.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following scholars defined religion in terms of a distinction between the sacred and the profane?
questions.explanation: Emile Durkheim, in his seminal work 'The Elementary Forms of Religious Life' (1912), defined religion based on the fundamental distinction between sacred and profane elements. For Durkheim, religion is a unified system of beliefs and practices related to sacred things - things set apart and forbidden - that unite adherents into a moral community or church. This sacred-profane dichotomy is the cornerstone of his sociological approach to religion.

questions.questionText: Which statement depicts the best definition of sustainable development?
options: It means optimal utilization of natural resources.
Sustainable use of natural resources without considering the needs of the future generation.
The present generation fulfills its needs while considering the needs of the future generation as well.
questions.explanation: Sustainable development balances current and future needs.

questions.questionText: Choose the WRONG statement regarding participant observation.
options: Participant observation can involve an array of data collection methods.
All participant observation is fieldwork and the reverse is also true.
Participant observation uses data collection methods like sampling.
Participant observation employs interviews, unobtrusive and checklist methods.
questions.explanation: The statement 'All participant observation is fieldwork and the reverse is also true' is incorrect. While participant observation is a form of fieldwork, not all fieldwork involves participant observation. Fieldwork can include non-participatory methods such as naturalistic observation, structured observation, or other data collection techniques where the researcher doesn't actively participate in the setting being studied.

questions.questionText: Select the best statement that explains social problems.
options: Social problems are integral to our daily lives.
All social problems acquire a perennial quality.
Social problems are never associated with us.
Social problems always have positive consequences.
questions.explanation: Social problems affect everyone in society.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a feature of globalization?
options: An increasing awareness of the world as a whole
The destruction of distance through communications technologies
The stretching of social relations beyond national boundaries
